docs.text: HILT ¶ HILT (Hardware-In-the-Loop Testing) is Python HIL testing with a pit of success: composable tests, guardrails that make a bad test hard to write, and an engine that won't let an unhandled failure pass silently. A Floor Technician categorizes a failure and starts the right recovery protocol without reading suite source; a developer writes the suite that makes that possible. Floor technicians: the station page is the Floor Technician guide . That is the URL that belongs on a station label. Suite authors: start with getting started , then the overview , idioms , and contracts . Public surface: API stability is the policy; the API reference is generated from the public names' docstrings. Inspector contributors: the target specification carries the terminal workflow that hilt inspect opens. Build this site locally with make docs . A broken cross-reference fails the gate. Nothing hosts it: GitLab renders every page from docs/ on main , and a release branch carries the built site under docs/site/ ( make docs-release ) so a station can open it from a clone without a network (#138).

docs.text: API Stability ¶ 1.0.0 is a promise. This document states what the promise covers, how version numbers carry it, how a name leaves the surface, and where every change is announced. The developer reads it to know which names are safe to build a station on and how much warning a change carries. Suites written for 1.0 keep running on every 1.x, so the Floor Technician's stations do not break on an upgrade. The self-tests hold the framework to this document ( tests/test_public_surface.py ): the reference table below and hilt.__all__ must name the same set, every example and every documented code block imports only that set from the package root, and hilt.__version__ reports the installed distribution. The public surface ¶ hilt.__all__ is the public surface. Everything else is private. A name is public if and only if it appears in hilt.__all__ . Import it from hilt ; the module a name is defined in is an implementation detail and may move without notice. from hilt import TestComponent is a promise; from hilt.base import TestComponent is not. The documented attributes, methods, parameters, and raised exceptions of a public name are part of the promise. "Documented" means named in this document, in docs/contracts.md , docs/idioms.md , docs/inspector-json.md , docs/junit-xml.md , or docs/hilt-check.md , or in the name's own docstring. A public object has no attribute of a private type. Every value a suite can read from a public object carries a public type, so the reader can follow every name back to its meaning. ScopedLogger is promised as its logging.LoggerAdapter base plus the documented scope and bread_crumbs additions. hilt.__version__ is public: the installed distribution's version string. The invariants in docs/contracts.md are promises in their own right. A change that weakens one is a breaking change even when no name moves. The records the framework emits ( result.json , timeline.jsonl , the point-in-time artifact envelope) are promised through their published JSON Schemas and format_version , under the policy in docs/inspector-json.md . Three environment variables are public configuration, and the framework reads no others: HILT_ARTIFACT_ROOT , the artifact root when TestUtils is given none; environment=DEBUG , which publishes every variable despite an env_allow or env_deny list and logs a warning saying so ( docs/inspector-json.md ); and SSH_AUTH_SOCK , the SSH agent get_shell and use_shell fall back to when no credential is given. The run environment as a whole is published as evidence under env_allow / env_deny , not read as configuration. The hilt run command line is public in two respects: its exit status contract ( 0 Pass, 1 Fail, 2 Aborted, 3 usage error) and its --json record, which is the result.json record under the same format_version policy ( docs/hilt-run.md ). The hilt.cli module behind it is not. The hilt new command line is public in two respects: the files it writes (a gated-PASS suite and a matching self-test stub) and its exit status ( 0 wrote the files, 3 usage error). The hilt.scaffold module behind it is not ( docs/hilt-new.md ). The hilt inspect command line is public in three respects: its selection rule (PATH is a run directory or its result.json ; no PATH opens the most recently modified result.json under HILT_ARTIFACT_ROOT , default artifacts/ ), its exit status ( 0 the Inspector was closed, 3 nothing to inspect, not a saved version-1 run, or a --suite that cannot be loaded), and the rule that the Re-Run tab executes only the suite the run recorded as suite_target or the one --suite names, never one derived from evidence. The screen behind it, hilt.inspector_app , and the re-run adapter, hilt.inspector_rerun , are not ( docs/inspector.md ). The hilt-check command line is public in two respects: its exit status contract and the rule codes it ships ( docs/hilt-check.md ). The Python API of the hilt_check package is not. Private, with no promise attached: Any name beginning with an underscore, at any depth. Every submodule path. hilt.lifecycle , hilt.routing , hilt.executor , hilt.timeline , hilt.mock , and the rest are the framework's organs; the self-tests import from them, suites do not. Annotation-only aliases that appear in signatures but are not exported ( WaitPredicate , HaltReason , ExecFn ). They are documented by their expansion. Directory and file names beneath the artifact root. TestComponent.log_path and the result pointer in the timeline are the API; the layout that produces them is not. The transports, RemoteInterface , SshInterface , and SerialInterface . A suite author never constructs a transport: TestUtils.use_shell and TestUtils.get_shell open an SSH connection and hand back a Shell ; TestUtils.use_serial and TestUtils.get_serial do the same for a console by device path, and their documented parameters are the promise the serial transport is reached through. Transport authors and the self-tests import hilt.remote , hilt.ssh , and hilt.serial directly; a transport contract for third parties is a design note of its own (issues #91, #93–#97). The Device API backends, DeviceApiInterface , HttpInterface , CoapInterface , and MockDeviceApi . A suite author never constructs one: TestUtils.get_http and TestUtils.get_coap open the session and hand back a DeviceApi . Self-tests import hilt.device_api directly. hilt.junit.JunitXml . The runner owns the reporter: hilt run --junit PATH is the promised way to a JUnit report. A harness adapter that imports hilt.junit directly does so without the promise, as docs/junit-xml.md says. The self-test fixtures, the loopback sshd, and MockTransport . A transport double for suite authors is a feature to be designed, not a side door into the test kit. Version numbers ¶ The distribution version follows Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 : MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH . Before 1.0.0 ( 0.y.z ) nothing is promised. A name may be renamed or removed in any release, without a deprecation period; the composition vocabulary ruling on issue #110 ( case and group removed outright, a hilt-check rule naming the replacement) is the precedent. Every such change still lands in CHANGELOG.md under the release that makes it, so the trail exists before the promise does. From 1.0.0 a release bumps exactly one component: Component Bumped when Examples MAJOR A promise is broken. A name leaves __all__ ; a documented parameter, attribute, or return type changes incompatibly; a contract in docs/contracts.md weakens; a format_version bumps; requires-python rises; a hilt-check rule code is removed or renamed. MINOR The surface grows or a deprecation is announced. A new name in __all__ ; a new optional keyword parameter; a new field on a record within its format_version ; a new hilt-check rule; a name marked deprecated. PATCH Behaviour is corrected without changing the surface. A bug fix that brings behaviour in line with a documented contract; a dependency bump that changes nothing a suite can observe; documentation. Two consequences the developer can rely on: A fix is not a break. When a documented contract and the code disagree, the document is the promise and the code is the bug. Correcting it is a PATCH even if a suite depended on the wrong behaviour. A format_version bump is a MAJOR. The Inspector and the harness that read a station's records are part of the station. A new record version that an installed consumer refuses is a break, whatever the Python surface did. Dependencies are private. asyncssh and anything else the framework imports may change major version in a MINOR or PATCH release as long as nothing a suite can observe changes; a dependency that becomes observable (a type in a public signature) becomes part of the promise at that moment and is documented as such. Deprecation ¶ A public name is never removed in the MAJOR line that introduced it. It is deprecated first, and removed no sooner than the next MAJOR release and no sooner than two MINOR releases after the deprecation was announced. Both conditions hold at once. Announcing a deprecation is one MR that does all of the following: The old spelling keeps working , with the documented behaviour, for the whole deprecation period. Calling it emits DeprecationWarning through warnings.warn with stacklevel=2 , so the warning points at the suite's line, not the framework's. The message names the replacement and the release that will remove the old spelling. The reference table marks it with Deprecated in x.y, removed in z.0 and the replacement, and the section that documents the name says the same. CHANGELOG.md records it under Deprecated for the release that announces it, and under Removed for the release that removes it. hilt-check gains a rule that flags the deprecated spelling and names the replacement, in the pattern of hilt/retired-names , so the finding reaches the developer's CI before it reaches a station log. The developer sees the warning in the self-tests of their own suite (pytest surfaces DeprecationWarning by default) and in hilt-check output; hilt run routes Python warnings through the run log so the station's console carries the notice as well. A removal at the next MAJOR deletes the code and the rule, moves the table row to the changelog's Removed list, and stops there: a removed name is not reused for something else within the following MAJOR line. The changelog ¶ CHANGELOG.md at the repository root follows Keep a Changelog : an Unreleased section at the top, one section per release below it, entries grouped under Added , Changed , Deprecated , Removed , Fixed , and Security . Every MR that changes a public name, a documented contract, a record format, or a hilt-check rule adds its line to Unreleased in the same MR. A release renames Unreleased to the version and date and opens a fresh Unreleased above it. The changelog is the announcement; the GitLab issue is the ruling behind it. Changing the surface ¶ A change to the public surface is a change to a promise, and the workflow in STANDARDS.md section 7 applies: it is raised as an issue for Ty's sign-off before its MR opens, stating how the change helps the developer help the Floor Technician. The MR then updates hilt.__all__ , the reference table below, the section that documents the name, and CHANGELOG.md together. The public-surface self-test refuses an MR that updates one without the others. Reference ¶ Every name in hilt.__all__ , what it is, and where its contract is written. Kind is checked against the object by the self-tests. Name Kind What it is Described in PASS constant The verdict. return PASS passes with no evidence; return PASS({...}) passes and carries the readings that prove it. docs/overview.md (Why HILT Rejects "Pass by Default"), docs/idioms.md (Evidence Travels With the Verdict), docs/contracts.md (Terminal State Contract) AfterEachContext class The narrow integration-hook context after a node settles: BeforeEachContext plus result . docs/idioms.md (Integration Hooks), docs/contracts.md (Integration Hook Contract) AfterEachHook type alias Callable[[AfterEachContext], Awaitable[None]] ; the after_each parameter of TestComponent.run . docs/idioms.md (Integration Hooks) ArpResolutionFailure class TestFailure raised when the resolver cannot map a MAC address to an IP. docs/idioms.md (ArpResolver — MAC to IP) ArpResolver class Resolve a MAC address to an IP through the node's current exec route; mac , resolve , reacquire , ping . docs/idioms.md (ArpResolver — MAC to IP, ArpResolver with Via-Routing) Artifact class Immutable point-in-time evidence ( name , type , data , timestamp ) for TestUtils.capture_artifact . docs/idioms.md (Point-in-Time Artifacts), docs/inspector-json.md BeforeEachContext class The narrow integration-hook context before a node runs: name , ancestor_names , bread_crumbs , logger , env . docs/idioms.md (Integration Hooks), docs/contracts.md (Integration Hook Contract) BeforeEachHook type alias Callable[[BeforeEachContext], Awaitable[None]] ; the before_each parameter of TestComponent.run . docs/idioms.md (Integration Hooks) CoapCode class Named CoAP response codes as dotted strings ( CONTENT is 2.05 , CHANGED is 2.04 , NOT_FOUND is 4.04 ). A CoAP DeviceResponse.status is one of these strings; from_wire renders a code byte the same way. docs/idioms.md (Device API — CoAP/HTTP), signed docs/hil/device-api.md ContractViolation class A developer bug: suite code did something the verdict contract forbids. Records as Fail with bug: true . docs/overview.md (Failure Taxonomy), docs/contracts.md (Failure Taxonomy Contract) DeviceApi class The session handle returned by TestUtils.get_http and TestUtils.get_coap ; request , scheme , base_url . docs/idioms.md (Device API — CoAP/HTTP), signed docs/hil/device-api.md DeviceApiOperationFailure class HiltError raised when a device-API transfer does not complete. Not a DUT verdict; HTTP 4xx/5xx is data on DeviceResponse . docs/idioms.md (Device API — CoAP/HTTP), signed docs/hil/device-api.md DeviceRequest class One resource operation: method , path , payload bytes or keyword-only json= , headers , retry declaration, evidence_headers . docs/contracts.md (Device API Contract), docs/idioms.md (Device API — CoAP/HTTP), signed docs/hil/device-api.md DeviceResponse class What a transfer returned: status , body bytes, headers ; json() and parse(response_type="json" or "yaml") decode explicitly. Status is data: an HTTP integer, or a CoAP dotted code ( 2.05 ). docs/contracts.md (Device API Contract), docs/idioms.md (Device API — CoAP/HTTP), signed docs/hil/device-api.md EvidenceViolation class ContractViolation raised by the child boundary when a verdict's evidence is not JSON, shadows a ctx key, or lacks a key @evidence declared; key . docs/idioms.md (Evidence Travels With the Verdict), docs/contracts.md (Evidence Contract) ExecResult class What a command produced: stdout , stderr , exit_code , truncated , captured_bytes . exec never throws. docs/contracts.md (Utils Contract) ExternalIntegrationFailure class A harness-level halt: an integration hook threw. Aborts the run. docs/overview.md (Failure Taxonomy), docs/contracts.md (Integration Hook Contract) Failure type alias The union of TestFailure , ExternalIntegrationFailure , OperatorInterrupt , and MissingVerdict ; the type of RunResult.failure . docs/contracts.md (Failure Taxonomy Contract) FrameworkContractViolation class A framework bug: the second layer of the guard, unreachable by design. Exported so a log line can be followed. docs/contracts.md (Failure Taxonomy Contract) HiltError class Root of the framework's exception taxonomy. docs/contracts.md (Failure Taxonomy Contract) JsonObject type alias dict[str, JsonValue] ; the shape of run_data , of a node's evidence , and of Artifact.data . docs/idioms.md (run_data — Automatic Structured Evidence) Measurement class One utils.measure call as recorded: name , value , unit , limits , in_limits , timestamp . Frozen; in_limits is evidence, never a verdict. value is None for a reading not taken, and such a reading is never inside its window. docs/measurements.md (The call) MissingVerdict class No verdict was produced: the test method returned something other than PASS . docs/overview.md (Failure Taxonomy), docs/contracts.md (Terminal State Contract) NodeType class StrEnum discriminator on RunResult.type and SummaryTreeNode.type : SUITE , TEST , PARALLEL , SEQUENCE ; the wire values are fixed by the result schema. docs/inspector-json.md (Version 1 result) OperatorInterrupt class A harness-level halt: the operator interrupted the run. Aborts the run. docs/overview.md (Failure Taxonomy), docs/contracts.md (Failure Taxonomy Contract) Phase class Ordered StrEnum of the six survey dispatch points, PRE_CONFIGURE through POST_CLEANUP ; the phases= selection of use_survey and the artifact-name prefix. docs/idioms.md (Constructor-Only Hooks), docs/contracts.md (Evidence Contract) RunEnv class The run environment on TestUtils.env : a read-only Mapping[str, str] plus text , require , port , int , and float , readers that Fail the run naming the bench variable to set. docs/idioms.md (TestUtils Injection), docs/hilt-run.md (Selecting the suite) RunResult class Self-contained evidence for one settled node: state , failure , timeout , ancestor_names , bread_crumbs , summary_tree , env , run_data , to_json . docs/idioms.md (RunResult Navigation), docs/inspector-json.md , docs/contracts.md (Evidence Contract) RunSignal class Read-only view of the halt signals affecting a node: fired , reason . TestUtils.signal . docs/idioms.md (TestUtils Injection) ScopedLogger class The per-node logger on TestUtils.logger and the hook contexts; a logging.LoggerAdapter with scope and bread_crumbs . docs/idioms.md (Logging), docs/contracts.md (Evidence Contract) Shell class The scoped exec handle returned by TestUtils.use_shell , TestUtils.get_shell , TestUtils.use_serial , and TestUtils.get_serial ; the via argument to all four. docs/idioms.md (SSH Device, SSH Tunneling), docs/utilities.md (Serial console), docs/contracts.md (Exec Routing Contract) Slot class StrEnum of the lifecycle positions the framework calls suite code from; RunResult.slot . docs/inspector-json.md (Version 1 result), docs/contracts.md (Lifecycle Contract) State class StrEnum of the three terminal states, PASS , FAIL , ABORTED ; RunResult.state . There is no fourth. docs/overview.md (The Three Terminal States), docs/contracts.md (Terminal State Contract) SummaryTreeNode class Plain recursive snapshot of the run tree on RunResult.summary_tree ; evidence , evidence_declared , to_json . docs/inspector-json.md (Summary tree) TestComponent class The atom: a claim about hardware and the procedure that produces its evidence. configure , build_suite , cleanup , run , main , test , sequence , parallel , use_survey , use_audit , name , log_path , run_data , and the redact_ctx class attribute. Optionally parameterized as TestComponent[CtxT] to type the suite's own context; the bare name keeps today's meaning. docs/overview.md (The Atom), docs/idioms.md , docs/contracts.md (Lifecycle Contract) TestFailure class A verdict of Fail: the hardware did not meet the spec. The exception a test method raises; evidence= carries the readings taken before it failed. docs/overview.md (Failure Taxonomy), docs/contracts.md (Failure Taxonomy Contract) TestUtils class The scoped service object handed to every lifecycle method: logger , ctx , env , signal , artifact_root , exec_route , exec , wait_for , capture_artifact , get_arp_resolver , use_shell , get_shell , use_serial , get_serial , get_http , get_coap , measure . Optionally parameterized as TestUtils[CtxT] so ctx returns the suite's declared shape. docs/idioms.md (TestUtils Injection), docs/utilities.md (Serial console), docs/contracts.md (Utils Contract) TimeoutEvidence class Structured evidence when a time budget cut a subtree: reason , declared , budget_seconds , elapsed_seconds , clock ; RunResult.timeout . docs/idioms.md (Time Budgets), docs/contracts.md (Time Budget Contract) Verdict class The return type of a test method: PASS or PASS(evidence) ; evidence . Generic in the evidence shape, so -> Verdict[MyEvidence] lets pyright check the payload. docs/overview.md (Why HILT Rejects "Pass by Default"), docs/idioms.md (Evidence Travels With the Verdict), docs/hilt-check.md ( hilt/unannotated-interface ) evidence function Decorator naming the keys a test method's PASS must carry: @evidence("k", ...) or @evidence(MyTypedDict) . Static at class definition. docs/idioms.md (Evidence Travels With the Verdict), docs/hilt-check.md ( hilt/evidence-fulfilled , hilt/evidence-shadows-ctx ) measure function Package-root spelling of utils.measure , resolved to the node whose configure() or test method is running and refused outside one. utils.measure is the documented home. docs/measurements.md (The package-root alias)

Name Kind What it is Described in PASS constant The verdict. return PASS passes with no evidence; return PASS({...}) passes and carries the readings that prove it. docs/overview.md (Why HILT Rejects "Pass by Default"), docs/idioms.md (Evidence Travels With the Verdict), docs/contracts.md (Terminal State Contract) AfterEachContext class The narrow integration-hook context after a node settles: BeforeEachContext plus result . docs/idioms.md (Integration Hooks), docs/contracts.md (Integration Hook Contract) AfterEachHook type alias Callable[[AfterEachContext], Awaitable[None]] ; the after_each parameter of TestComponent.run . docs/idioms.md (Integration Hooks) ArpResolutionFailure class TestFailure raised when the resolver cannot map a MAC address to an IP. docs/idioms.md (ArpResolver — MAC to IP) ArpResolver class Resolve a MAC address to an IP through the node's current exec route; mac , resolve , reacquire , ping . docs/idioms.md (ArpResolver — MAC to IP, ArpResolver with Via-Routing) Artifact class Immutable point-in-time evidence ( name , type , data , timestamp ) for TestUtils.capture_artifact . docs/idioms.md (Point-in-Time Artifacts), docs/inspector-json.md BeforeEachContext class The narrow integration-hook context before a node runs: name , ancestor_names , bread_crumbs , logger , env . docs/idioms.md (Integration Hooks), docs/contracts.md (Integration Hook Contract) BeforeEachHook type alias Callable[[BeforeEachContext], Awaitable[None]] ; the before_each parameter of TestComponent.run . docs/idioms.md (Integration Hooks) CoapCode class Named CoAP response codes as dotted strings ( CONTENT is 2.05 , CHANGED is 2.04 , NOT_FOUND is 4.04 ). A CoAP DeviceResponse.status is one of these strings; from_wire renders a code byte the same way. docs/idioms.md (Device API — CoAP/HTTP), signed docs/hil/device-api.md ContractViolation class A developer bug: suite code did something the verdict contract forbids. Records as Fail with bug: true . docs/overview.md (Failure Taxonomy), docs/contracts.md (Failure Taxonomy Contract) DeviceApi class The session handle returned by TestUtils.get_http and TestUtils.get_coap ; request , scheme , base_url . docs/idioms.md (Device API — CoAP/HTTP), signed docs/hil/device-api.md DeviceApiOperationFailure class HiltError raised when a device-API transfer does not complete. TestUtils.signal . docs/idioms.md (TestUtils Injection) ScopedLogger class The per-node logger on TestUtils.logger and the hook contexts; a logging.LoggerAdapter with scope and bread_crumbs . docs/idioms.md (Logging), docs/contracts.md (Evidence Contract) Shell class The scoped exec handle returned by TestUtils.use_shell , TestUtils.get_shell , TestUtils.use_serial , and TestUtils.get_serial ; the via argument to all four. docs/idioms.md (SSH Device, SSH Tunneling), docs/utilities.md (Serial console), docs/contracts.md (Exec Routing Contract) Slot class StrEnum of the lifecycle positions the framework calls suite code from; RunResult.slot . docs/inspector-json.md (Version 1 result), docs/contracts.md (Lifecycle Contract) State class StrEnum of the three terminal states, PASS , FAIL , ABORTED ; RunResult.state . docs.text: API reference ¶ The public surface is hilt.__all__ . Import these names from hilt ; the module a name is defined in is an implementation detail. The policy is API stability . PASS module-attribute ¶ PASS : Verdict [ Never ] = Verdict () The verdict. return PASS passes with no evidence; return PASS({...}) passes and carries the readings that prove it. AfterEachContext dataclass ¶ AfterEachContext ( name : str , ancestor_names : tuple [ str , ... ], bread_crumbs : str , logger : LoggerAdapter [ Logger ], env : Mapping [ str , str ], result : RunResult , ) Bases: BeforeEachContext The narrow integration context plus this node's completed result. AfterEachHook ¶ AfterEachHook = Callable [ [ AfterEachContext ], Awaitable [ None ] ] ArpResolutionFailure ¶ ArpResolutionFailure ( message : str , * , mac : str , host : str ) Bases: HiltError The resolver could not map a MAC address to an IP. This is not a TestFailure . That is deliberate: Uncaught in a test method or configure , the child boundary classifies it as a developer bug. The suite did not model this failure mode at all. Caught and re-raised as TestFailure , the author acknowledged the mode and chose the verdict shape: the device did not appear on the network. Catching this does not tell you why the ARP entry is missing — dead NIC, unplugged cable, hungry switch, DHCP failure, or a gateway that has not seen traffic from the target yet. No amount of code can distinguish those. Hardware versus infrastructure is the human triager's call from logs, survey artifacts, and the bench. Do not write code that pretends to know. If this extended TestFailure , an uncaught miss would land in Fail and look like a modeled hardware verdict, hiding that the author never handled the mode. Record the MAC that could not be resolved and the host that was asked. Parameters: Name Type Description Default message str What failed, in the FT's language. required mac str The normalised MAC that was missing from the table. required host str Routing label of the host whose ARP table was read ( "local" , "via 10.0.0.1" , …). required ArpResolver ¶ ArpResolver ( * , mac : str , ping_count : int = 1 , exec_fn : ExecFn | None = None , logger : ScopedLogger | None = None , cache_key : str | None = None ) Resolve a MAC address to an IP through the node's current exec route. resolve() returns a plain dict suitable for spreading into configure() 's return value. ping(utils) is a gated reachability claim. reacquire(utils) forces a fresh table read after a reboot, flash, or DHCP churn and returns the new IP; the resolver remembers it, so a later ping(utils) dials the address it last resolved. Ctx is read-only after configure() , so the address that moves lives in the resolver, and a test that wants it on the record carries it as evidence: PASS({"ip": ip}) . Raises: Type Description ArpResolutionFailure The MAC is missing from the table, or /proc/net/arp is unreadable. This is not a TestFailure . Uncaught it is a developer bug — the suite did not model the failure mode. Catch it and re-raise as TestFailure to make "the device did not appear on the network" a verdict. Hardware versus infrastructure remains the triager's call. RuntimeError resolve() was called on an instance that was not created through utils.get_arp_resolver() . ValueError mac does not contain 12 hex digits, or ping_count < 1. Bind a MAC. Authors go through utils.get_arp_resolver() , not this. Parameters: Name Type Description Default mac str Device MAC in any usual form (colons, dashes, or bare hex). required ping_count int ICMP packets per ping() . Must be at least 1. 1 exec_fn ExecFn | None Route used to read the ARP table. Injected by get_arp_resolver . None logger ScopedLogger | None Scoped logger for the resolve/reacquire lines. None cache_key str | None Routing label identifying which host's table this is. None mac property ¶ mac : str The normalised colon-separated lowercase MAC this resolver owns. reset_caches classmethod ¶ reset_caches () -> None Drop every ARP table cache. Self-tests call this between cases. resolve async ¶ resolve () -> dict [ str , str ] Refresh a stale cache and return {"ip": ...} for this MAC. Zero-arg: uses the exec and cache key get_arp_resolver bound. Raises if this instance was constructed without that scope. reacquire async ¶ reacquire ( utils : TestUtils ) -> str Force a fresh ARP read and return the new IP. Call from a test method after anything that may have changed the IP. The cache key stays the resolver's — that is the host whose table holds this MAC — while the command runs through the child's utils.exec . The resolver's shared table now holds the new address, so ping(utils) on any resolver for this MAC dials it; carry it as evidence on the verdict if the Floor Technician should see it. ping async ¶ ping ( utils : TestUtils ) -> Verdict Reachability claim against this MAC's last resolved IP. The address is read from the resolver's table for this MAC, which resolve() and reacquire() both refresh, and falls back to utils.ctx["ip"] for a context that was seeded without a resolve. Uses the child's exec and logger. Packet loss and a missing stats line are TestFailure . Duplicate replies ( received > transmitted ) still count as success — the host answered. A missing IP (resolve never ran) is ArpResolutionFailure . Artifact dataclass ¶ Artifact ( name : str , type : str , data : object , timestamp : datetime = ( lambda : datetime . now ( UTC ))(), ) Describe point-in-time evidence without exposing a file-writing operation. Persistence belongs exclusively to :meth: TestUtils.capture_artifact ; keeping this value immutable and write-free makes it impossible for the public framework surface to create an artifact that lacks its chronological log pointer. to_json ¶ to_json () -> dict [ str , object ] Return the versioned JSON shape persisted by the framework. BeforeEachContext dataclass ¶ BeforeEachContext ( name : str , ancestor_names : tuple [ str , ... ], bread_crumbs : str , logger : LoggerAdapter [ Logger ], env : Mapping [ str , str ], ) External-coordination context that cannot exercise the target hardware. BeforeEachHook ¶ BeforeEachHook = Callable [ [ BeforeEachContext ], Awaitable [ None ] ] CoapCode ¶ Dotted CoAP response codes, the form a record can carry. A CoAP DeviceResponse.status is one of these strings ( "2.05" ), never the wire integer class << 5 | detail . HTTP status stays an int . Compare with response.status == CoapCode.CONTENT and put response.status on the evidence as-is: it is already the text a reader sees. from_wire is how the transport, and a claim that still holds a code byte, spells that integer. from_wire staticmethod ¶ from_wire ( code : int ) -> str Render a CoAP code byte as class.detail ( 69 becomes "2.05" ). Raises: Type Description ValueError code is not an integer in 0-255. Booleans are refused. ContractViolation ¶ ContractViolation ( node : str , detail : str | None = None , cause : BaseException | None = None , ) Bases: TestFailure A developer bug: suite code did something the verdict contract forbids. Raised by the framework, never by suite code. It is a TestFailure subclass on purpose — the node lands in Fail — but it carries a banner so nobody mistakes a broken test for a broken unit. Banner the violation with the node it happened in. Parameters: Name Type Description Default node str Name of the node whose contract was violated. required detail str | None What specifically went wrong. Defaults to the general form. None cause BaseException | None The original exception, preserved verbatim for the artifact. None is_bug property ¶ is_bug : bool A contract violation is always a developer bug, never a device fault. escaped classmethod ¶ escaped ( node : str , error : BaseException ) -> ContractViolation Banner an exception that is not a verdict and escaped suite code. The author neither returned PASS nor raised TestFailure , so the default "return PASS or raise TestFailure" advice would misdescribe what happened. The detail names the exception type and message — the thing the reader has to fix — and the original stays on cause for the artifact. to_json ¶ to_json () -> dict [ str , Any ] Carry banner, node, and cause so the record names who is at fault and where. DeviceApi ¶ DeviceApi ( backend : DeviceApiInterface ) Author-facing handle from get_http / get_coap . Suite authors do not construct this. request returns a typed response; HTTP 4xx is data, not an exception. The framework owns connect, retry, and the closed-session halt. One handle carries one request at a time: parallel leaves sharing it queue in call order, so a latency measured around request on a shared handle includes the wait for siblings. Wrap an already-connected backend. Framework and self-tests only. scheme property ¶ scheme : str Scheme this handle was bound to. base_url property ¶ base_url : str Declared origin. request async ¶ request ( req : DeviceRequest ) -> DeviceResponse Perform req on this session. See :class: DeviceRequest . DeviceApiOperationFailure ¶ DeviceApiOperationFailure ( message : str , * , handle : str , operation : str , method : str , path : str , ceiling : float | None = None ) Bases: HiltError A device-API transfer did not complete. This is not a DUT verdict. Uncaught in a test method or configure , the child boundary classifies it as a developer bug: the suite did not model this failure mode. Caught and re-raised as TestFailure , the author chose the verdict. A well-formed HTTP 4xx/5xx is not this error — that status is data on DeviceResponse . Record the handle, operation, and ceiling that did not complete. Parameters: Name Type Description Default message str What failed, in the FT's language. required handle str Scheme plus base URL of the session. required operation str request , connect , or close . required method str HTTP/CoAP method, or empty when the operation has none. required path str Resource path, or empty when the operation has none. required ceiling float | None Backend-declared seconds bound, when one expired. None DeviceRequest dataclass ¶ DeviceRequest ( method : DeviceMethod , path : str , payload : bytes | None = None , headers : Mapping [ str , str ] = MappingProxyType ({}), retries : int = 0 , retry_delay : float = 0.05 , retry_non_idempotent : bool = False , timeout : float | None = None , evidence_headers : frozenset [ str ] = frozenset (), * , json : InitVar [ Any ] = _NO_JSON ) One resource operation: method, path, optional payload, optional headers. Path is relative to the handle's base URL. Use payload for raw bytes or keyword-only json for a JSON value, including None (JSON null). JSON is encoded once as UTF-8 and adds Content-Type: application/json unless a content type was supplied. Supplying both bodies raises ValueError ; unserializable or non-finite JSON is refused at construction. retries counts extra application-level attempts after the first; the default is zero. Attempt logs withhold every header value unless the name is in evidence_headers . DeviceResponse dataclass ¶ DeviceResponse ( status : int | str , body : bytes , headers : Mapping [ str , str ] = MappingProxyType ({}), ) The bytes and status a transfer actually returned. HTTP 4xx/5xx and CoAP 4.xx/5.xx are fields here, not exceptions. An HTTP status is the integer. A CoAP status is the dotted code ( "2.05" , :class: CoapCode ). headers carries HTTP headers or CoAP options as strings. body is the payload bytes. Parsing is opt-in through json() or parse(response_type=...) ; a parsing error never changes the transfer's status or raw bytes. json ¶ json () -> Any Decode the body as JSON, independent of status and content type. Raises json.JSONDecodeError for malformed JSON and UnicodeDecodeError for invalid encoding. No fallback value is invented. parse ¶ parse ( response_type : Literal [ "json" , "yaml" ] = "json" , ) -> Any Decode the body in the explicitly selected format; default is JSON. YAML uses yaml.safe_load and requires the hilt-core[yaml] extra. Parser errors propagate unchanged; an unknown response_type raises ValueError . Parsing never sends a request or changes the response. EvidenceViolation ¶ EvidenceViolation ( node : str , * , key : str , reason : str ) Bases: ContractViolation The evidence a verdict carried broke the evidence contract. Three reasons, one class, so the Floor Technician reads one banner and the message names the key: the value cannot be carried as JSON, the key shadows a ctx entry or the reserved measurements slot, or @evidence declared the key and PASS did not carry it. A pass without its declared evidence is not a pass: the node lands in Fail under the contract-violation banner and no hardware verdict is forged (issue #118). Name the offending key and why it offends. Parameters: Name Type Description Default node str Name of the leaf whose verdict carried the evidence. required key str The evidence key at fault. required reason str One of the three sentences above, in the FT's language. required not_carried classmethod ¶ not_carried ( node : str , key : str ) -> EvidenceViolation @evidence declared key and PASS did not carry it. not_serializable classmethod ¶ not_serializable ( node : str , key : str ) -> EvidenceViolation The value under key cannot be carried as JSON. shadows_context classmethod ¶ shadows_context ( node : str , key : str ) -> EvidenceViolation key is already a ctx entry or the reserved measurements slot. to_json ¶ to_json () -> dict [ str , Any ] Carry the offending key so the record names the collision, not just the class. ExecResult dataclass ¶ ExecResult ( stdout : str , stderr : str , exit_code : int , truncated : bool = False , captured_bytes : int = 0 , ) What a host command produced. A non-zero exit_code is evidence, not an exception. -1 means the process was killed by a signal, or was aborted before an exit status existed. truncated means stdout+stderr together hit the output budget; captured_bytes is how much was kept. Existing callers that omit both still construct a result. settled classmethod ¶ settled ( stdout : str | bytes | None , stderr : str | bytes | None , exit_status : int | None , * , truncated : bool = False , captured_bytes : int | None = None ) -> ExecResult Settle raw transport output into a result. Output arrives as whatever the transport produced — bytes (decoded UTF-8 with replacement), str , or nothing (empty). An exit_status of None or below zero means no real status exists — signal kill, or abort before an exit status — and settles as -1 . Every transport builds its results here, so the -1 contract cannot drift between them. Truncation is evidence, not an exception: the marker and byte count ride on the same result. ExternalIntegrationFailure ¶ ExternalIntegrationFailure ( hook : HookName , cause : BaseException ) Bases: HiltError A harness-level halt: an integration hook threw. One instance plays three structurally identical roles — the failure recorded on the Aborted node, the reason carried by the run-level abort, and the exception raised at the boundary that noticed. One class, three roles, zero wrapper layers. Do not introduce a wrapper: this type is never rewrapped by an ancestor, because the integrator must see their own error, not the framework's opinion of it. The original thrown value survives verbatim on cause so a DB driver error or a network rejection crosses the framework boundary unrebranded. Carry the integrator's error across the framework without rebranding it. Parameters: Name Type Description Default hook HookName Which hook threw — before_each or after_each . required cause BaseException The integrator's original exception, preserved verbatim. required is_bug property ¶ is_bug : bool False: the integrator's system failed, not the suite and not the framework. to_json ¶ to_json () -> dict [ str , Any ] JSON-safe snapshot for the run artifact. Never raises. Failure ¶ Failure = TestFailure | HaltReason | MissingVerdict Everything that can be recorded on a settled node. Pass records nothing. FrameworkContractViolation ¶ FrameworkContractViolation ( node : str , detail : str | None = None , cause : BaseException | None = None , ) Bases: ContractViolation A framework bug — the second layer of the guard, and unreachable by design. If this ever appears in a log, hilt itself is wrong. Its banner is distinct from the developer layer so the FT knows to escalate to the maintainers rather than to the suite author. Banner a framework bug and name the maintainer escalation. Parameters: Name Type Description Default node str Name of the node whose contract was violated. required detail str | None What specifically went wrong. A rule-only detail is completed with the maintainer escalation so the author-facing string names the fix. Defaults to the general form. None cause BaseException | None The original exception, preserved verbatim for the artifact. None HiltError ¶ Bases: Exception Root of the framework's own exception taxonomy. Catching this catches everything hilt raises deliberately and nothing a suite author raises by accident. A failure recorded at the child boundary is bound to the run's redactions (issue #154): from then on str() , repr() , and to_json() mask every secret the suite declared through redact_ctx , so a TestFailure that was handed a session credential as its received value renders it as <REDACTED> on every surface. Every to_json in the taxonomy is wrapped at class creation, so a subclass need not know the masking exists. JsonObject ¶ JsonObject = dict [ str , JsonValue ] Measurement dataclass ¶ Measurement ( name : str , value : int | float | None , unit : str | None , limits : Limits | None , in_limits : bool | None , timestamp : datetime , ) One utils.measure call, exactly as recorded. Frozen because the record is sealed with the node: a consumer keys a time series on name together with the node path, so a value that could change after the call would corrupt the series it belongs to. in_limits is None when the reading was recorded without a window, True or False otherwise; it is a recorded fact, and the verdict is decided elsewhere. A reading that was not taken has value=None . It is never inside its window, so in_limits is False when limits were given: a gate written on the window fails the claim however it is spelled, and the claim decides what a missing reading means. Without limits it is None , as for any trend reading. Attributes: Name Type Description name str The identity of the quantity, unique within the node. value int | float | None The reading, an int or a finite float ; None when the suite tried to take it and could not. unit str | None The developer's label for the reading, or None for a dimensionless count. Never validated, never converted. limits Limits | None The inclusive (low, high) window, or None when none was given. in_limits bool | None Whether value sits inside limits ; False for a reading not taken against a window; None without limits. timestamp datetime When the reading was recorded, timezone-aware UTC. to_json ¶ to_json () -> JsonObject Return the version-1 record shape from docs/measurements.md . limits becomes an object with explicit low and high keys rather than a bare array so that an open side reads as null by name, and the timestamp takes the timeline's own UTC Z form so one clock reads across both records. MissingVerdict ¶ MissingVerdict ( node : str , returned : object ) Bases: HiltError No verdict was produced: the node returned something other than the sentinel. A None fall-through or an explicit wrong value. Still a developer contract violation, logged as loudly as one — but not a failure, and deliberately not a TestFailure . The node rendered no verdict, and the framework will not forge Fail or Pass on its behalf. Renders node-local Aborted; siblings are unaffected, because one author's missing return must not take down a seventy-DUT run. Record the non-verdict a node returned. Parameters: Name Type Description Default node str Name of the node that returned without a verdict. required returned object The value it returned instead of PASS. required is_bug property ¶ is_bug : bool True: the absence of a verdict is always broken code, never broken hardware. to_json ¶ to_json () -> dict [ str , Any ] JSON-safe snapshot for the run artifact. Never raises. NodeType ¶ Bases: StrEnum Inspector discriminator for each framework-owned node shape. The wire values are the composition vocabulary: the word the developer wrote in build_suite is the word the Floor Technician reads in the tree (issue #111). OperatorInterrupt ¶ OperatorInterrupt ( signum : int ) Bases: HiltError A harness-level halt: the operator interrupted the run. One instance is the failure recorded on every Aborted node and the reason carried by the run-level abort. It is not a TestFailure and not an integration-hook failure: the recovery is "the operator stopped the rack." Name the operator and the signal that stopped the run. Parameters: Name Type Description Default signum int The POSIX signal number ( SIGINT , SIGTERM ). required is_bug property ¶ is_bug : bool False: the operator stopped the run, not the suite and not the hardware. to_json ¶ to_json () -> dict [ str , Any ] JSON-safe snapshot for the run artifact. Never raises. Phase ¶ Bases: StrEnum The six survey dispatch points of one node lifecycle, in the order they occur. The values are the artifact-name prefixes the Evidence Contract already publishes ( pre-configure-1 ), so naming a phase in code names it in the run directory. Members order by declaration, not by string: Phase.PRE_TEST < Phase.POST_TEST holds. Order is not reach. After a failed configure the engine skips post-configure, pre-test, and post-test and still fires pre-cleanup and post-cleanup, so a survey scheduled "post-configure onward" guards the device with utils.exec_route , not with the phase. RunEnv ¶ RunEnv ( values : Mapping [ str , str ]) Bases: Mapping [ str , str ] The run environment: a read-only mapping with readers that Fail the run. Contract It is the filtered, immutable snapshot TestUtils.env publishes on every RunResult . get , in , [] , and iteration behave as on any mapping. text(name) trims the value and treats blank as unset. A bench script that exports TARGET_PASSWORD="" means "no password", not "the empty password". require(name) raises TestFailure naming the variable to set. Called from configure , that is the "did not reach a testable state" verdict: the run Fails before any claim runs, and the message is the operator's instruction. port(name, default=22) parses an integer in 1-65535 and raises TestFailure for anything else, so a bench typo is reported as the variable rather than surfacing later as a transport error. int(name, default=) and float(name, default=) do the same for a number. Unset or blank uses default when one was passed, and otherwise Fails naming the variable. A textual observation is evidence on the verdict, not a measurement; NaN is a bug in the suite, not a missing reading. required unit str | None Free label such as "V" or "ms" , or None for a dimensionless count. Never validated, never converted. None limits Limits | None Inclusive (low, high) window with None on an open side, or None to record for trend with in_limits unset. None Returns: Type Description Measurement The frozen Measurement exactly as recorded. Raises: Type Description ContractViolation When an argument is refused, when the name was already recorded in this node, or when the call comes from outside configure() or the test method. TimeoutEvidence dataclass ¶ TimeoutEvidence ( reason : Literal [ "timeout" ], declared : TimeBudgetName , budget_seconds : float , elapsed_seconds : float , clock : str , ) Structured evidence emitted when a time-budget clock cuts a subtree. to_json ¶ to_json () -> JsonObject Return the stable Inspector representation. Verdict ¶ The value that means "this node passed", with or without evidence. Contract Exactly one bare instance exists per interpreter. Verdict() returns it; copying, deep-copying, and unpickling all return it. It is the value bound to PASS . PASS(evidence) mints a verdict that carries a detached copy of evidence . It is a distinct object, so identity with PASS is never the check: the child boundary asks isinstance(result, Verdict) . evidence is read-only. The boundary copies it into run_data after checking every entry; a carrying verdict cannot be edited after it is returned. repr() is the bare word PASS , or PASS({...}) for a carrying verdict, so logs and artifacts read as the FT expects rather than showing an address. The type parameter is the evidence shape. A method annotated -> Verdict[MyEvidence] with a TypedDict has its PASS({...}) payload checked against that shape by pyright; the bare -> Verdict accepts any mapping. evidence property ¶ evidence : Mapping [ str , object ] | None The readings this verdict carries, or None for the bare PASS . evidence ¶ @evidence : the readings a test method promises to carry on PASS . A test method is a function from utils.ctx to a verdict. The decorator is the method's return signature: it names the keys a pass must carry, beside the code that keeps the promise. It annotates and registers nothing; build_suite still names and binds the method. The declaration is fixed at class definition and never computed at run time: pass criteria that vary by SKU or fixture are a leaf argument or a different leaf, decided before build_suite runs (issue #118). The child boundary holds PASS to the declaration: a declared key the payload does not carry is a ContractViolation naming the leaf and the key. Extra keys are allowed; the declaration is a floor. TestFailure is not held to it, since a failure may fire before every reading was taken. An undecorated method may still return PASS(payload) ; the payload is recorded unchecked. Two spellings:: @evidence("output_voltage_v") async def _check_voltage(self, utils: TestUtils) -> Verdict: ... class VoltageEvidence(TypedDict): output_voltage_v: float @evidence(VoltageEvidence) async def _check_voltage(self, utils: TestUtils) -> Verdict[VoltageEvidence]: ... The TypedDict form declares its required keys at run time and lets pyright check the PASS({...}) payload against the shape at write time. evidence ¶ evidence ( * keys : str , ) -> Callable [[ _Method [ P , R ]], _Method [ P , R ]] evidence ( shape : type [ E ], ) -> Callable [ [ _Method [ P , Verdict [ E ]]], _Method [ P , Verdict [ E ]] ] evidence ( * keys : str | type [ Mapping [ str , object ]] ) -> Callable [[ Any ], Any ] Declare the evidence keys a PASS from the decorated test method must carry. Parameters: Name Type Description Default *keys str | type [ Mapping [ str , object ]] String keys, or exactly one TypedDict class whose required keys are the declaration. () Raises: Type Description TypeError The declaration is empty, mixes the two spellings, repeats a key, or names a class that is not a TypedDict . declared_evidence ¶ declared_evidence ( fn : object ) -> tuple [ str , ... ] | None The keys fn was decorated to carry on PASS , or None when undeclared. measure ¶ measure ( name : str , value : int | float | None , * , unit : str | None = None , limits : Limits | None = None ) -> Measurement Record a measurement on the node whose configure() or test method is running. The package-root spelling of utils.measure (issue #85, Ty's condition): the same signature, the same rules, the same record. It exists so from hilt import measure reads naturally in a suite; utils.measure remains the documented home. Outside a running slot there is no node to record against, so the call is refused rather than recorded somewhere surprising. Parameters: Name Type Description Default name str Non-empty identity of the quantity, unique within the node. required value int | float | None An int or finite float , or None for a reading not taken. required unit str | None Free label such as "V" or "ms" , or None for a count. None limits Limits | None Inclusive (low, high) window, None on an open side, or None . None Returns: Type Description Measurement The frozen Measurement , with in_limits already decided. Raises: Type Description MeasurementUnbound When no node's configure() or test method is executing in the current task.

docs.text: ArpResolutionFailure ( message : str , * , mac : str , host : str ) Bases: HiltError The resolver could not map a MAC address to an IP. This is not a TestFailure . That is deliberate: Uncaught in a test method or configure , the child boundary classifies it as a developer bug. The suite did not model this failure mode at all. Caught and re-raised as TestFailure , the author acknowledged the mode and chose the verdict shape: the device did not appear on the network. Catching this does not tell you why the ARP entry is missing — dead NIC, unplugged cable, hungry switch, DHCP failure, or a gateway that has not seen traffic from the target yet. No amount of code can distinguish those. Hardware versus infrastructure is the human triager's call from logs, survey artifacts, and the bench. Do not write code that pretends to know. If this extended TestFailure , an uncaught miss would land in Fail and look like a modeled hardware verdict, hiding that the author never handled the mode. Record the MAC that could not be resolved and the host that was asked. Parameters: Name Type Description Default message str What failed, in the FT's language. required mac str The normalised MAC that was missing from the table. required host str Routing label of the host whose ARP table was read ( "local" , "via 10.0.0.1" , …). required
docs.title: ArpResolutionFailure

docs.text: ArpResolver ( * , mac : str , ping_count : int = 1 , exec_fn : ExecFn | None = None , logger : ScopedLogger | None = None , cache_key : str | None = None ) Resolve a MAC address to an IP through the node's current exec route. resolve() returns a plain dict suitable for spreading into configure() 's return value. ping(utils) is a gated reachability claim. reacquire(utils) forces a fresh table read after a reboot, flash, or DHCP churn and returns the new IP; the resolver remembers it, so a later ping(utils) dials the address it last resolved. Ctx is read-only after configure() , so the address that moves lives in the resolver, and a test that wants it on the record carries it as evidence: PASS({"ip": ip}) . Raises: Type Description ArpResolutionFailure The MAC is missing from the table, or /proc/net/arp is unreadable. This is not a TestFailure . Uncaught it is a developer bug — the suite did not model the failure mode. Catch it and re-raise as TestFailure to make "the device did not appear on the network" a verdict. Hardware versus infrastructure remains the triager's call. RuntimeError resolve() was called on an instance that was not created through utils.get_arp_resolver() . ValueError mac does not contain 12 hex digits, or ping_count < 1. Bind a MAC. Authors go through utils.get_arp_resolver() , not this. Parameters: Name Type Description Default mac str Device MAC in any usual form (colons, dashes, or bare hex). required ping_count int ICMP packets per ping() . Must be at least 1. 1 exec_fn ExecFn | None Route used to read the ARP table. Injected by get_arp_resolver . None logger ScopedLogger | None Scoped logger for the resolve/reacquire lines. None cache_key str | None Routing label identifying which host's table this is. None
docs.title: ArpResolver

docs.text: mac : str The normalised colon-separated lowercase MAC this resolver owns.
docs.title: mac

docs.text: reset_caches () -> None Drop every ARP table cache. Self-tests call this between cases.
docs.title: reset_caches

docs.text: resolve () -> dict [ str , str ] Refresh a stale cache and return {"ip": ...} for this MAC. Zero-arg: uses the exec and cache key get_arp_resolver bound. Raises if this instance was constructed without that scope.
docs.title: resolve

docs.text: reacquire ( utils : TestUtils ) -> str Force a fresh ARP read and return the new IP. Call from a test method after anything that may have changed the IP. The cache key stays the resolver's — that is the host whose table holds this MAC — while the command runs through the child's utils.exec . The resolver's shared table now holds the new address, so ping(utils) on any resolver for this MAC dials it; carry it as evidence on the verdict if the Floor Technician should see it.
docs.title: reacquire

docs.text: ping ( utils : TestUtils ) -> Verdict Reachability claim against this MAC's last resolved IP. The address is read from the resolver's table for this MAC, which resolve() and reacquire() both refresh, and falls back to utils.ctx["ip"] for a context that was seeded without a resolve. Uses the child's exec and logger. Packet loss and a missing stats line are TestFailure . Duplicate replies ( received > transmitted ) still count as success — the host answered. A missing IP (resolve never ran) is ArpResolutionFailure .
docs.title: ping

Banner the violation with the node it happened in. One handle carries one request at a time: parallel leaves sharing it queue in call order, so a latency measured around request on a shared handle includes the wait for siblings. Wrap an already-connected backend. Framework and self-tests only.

Caught and re-raised as TestFailure , the author chose the verdict. A well-formed HTTP 4xx/5xx is not this error — that status is data on DeviceResponse . docs.text: DeviceRequest ( method : DeviceMethod , path : str , payload : bytes | None = None , headers : Mapping [ str , str ] = MappingProxyType ({}), retries : int = 0 , retry_delay : float = 0.05 , retry_non_idempotent : bool = False , timeout : float | None = None , evidence_headers : frozenset [ str ] = frozenset (), * , json : InitVar [ Any ] = _NO_JSON ) One resource operation: method, path, optional payload, optional headers. Path is relative to the handle's base URL. Use payload for raw bytes or keyword-only json for a JSON value, including None (JSON null). JSON is encoded once as UTF-8 and adds Content-Type: application/json unless a content type was supplied. Supplying both bodies raises ValueError ; unserializable or non-finite JSON is refused at construction. retries counts extra application-level attempts after the first; the default is zero. Attempt logs withhold every header value unless the name is in evidence_headers .

docs.text: DeviceResponse ( status : int | str , body : bytes , headers : Mapping [ str , str ] = MappingProxyType ({}), ) The bytes and status a transfer actually returned. HTTP 4xx/5xx and CoAP 4.xx/5.xx are fields here, not exceptions. An HTTP status is the integer. A CoAP status is the dotted code ( "2.05" , :class: CoapCode ). headers carries HTTP headers or CoAP options as strings. body is the payload bytes. Parsing is opt-in through json() or parse(response_type=...) ; a parsing error never changes the transfer's status or raw bytes.

docs.text: EvidenceViolation ( node : str , * , key : str , reason : str ) Bases: ContractViolation The evidence a verdict carried broke the evidence contract. Three reasons, one class, so the Floor Technician reads one banner and the message names the key: the value cannot be carried as JSON, the key shadows a ctx entry or the reserved measurements slot, or @evidence declared the key and PASS did not carry it. A pass without its declared evidence is not a pass: the node lands in Fail under the contract-violation banner and no hardware verdict is forged (issue #118). Name the offending key and why it offends. Parameters: Name Type Description Default node str Name of the leaf whose verdict carried the evidence. required key str The evidence key at fault. required reason str One of the three sentences above, in the FT's language. required

docs.text: ExecResult ( stdout : str , stderr : str , exit_code : int , truncated : bool = False , captured_bytes : int = 0 , ) What a host command produced. A non-zero exit_code is evidence, not an exception. -1 means the process was killed by a signal, or was aborted before an exit status existed. truncated means stdout+stderr together hit the output budget; captured_bytes is how much was kept. Existing callers that omit both still construct a result.
docs.title: ExecResult

docs.text: settled ( stdout : str | bytes | None , stderr : str | bytes | None , exit_status : int | None , * , truncated : bool = False , captured_bytes : int | None = None ) -> ExecResult Settle raw transport output into a result. Output arrives as whatever the transport produced — bytes (decoded UTF-8 with replacement), str , or nothing (empty). An exit_status of None or below zero means no real status exists — signal kill, or abort before an exit status — and settles as -1 . Every transport builds its results here, so the -1 contract cannot drift between them. Truncation is evidence, not an exception: the marker and byte count ride on the same result.
docs.title: settled

docs.text: ExternalIntegrationFailure ( hook : HookName , cause : BaseException ) Bases: HiltError A harness-level halt: an integration hook threw. One instance plays three structurally identical roles — the failure recorded on the Aborted node, the reason carried by the run-level abort, and the exception raised at the boundary that noticed. One class, three roles, zero wrapper layers. Do not introduce a wrapper: this type is never rewrapped by an ancestor, because the integrator must see their own error, not the framework's opinion of it. The original thrown value survives verbatim on cause so a DB driver error or a network rejection crosses the framework boundary unrebranded. Carry the integrator's error across the framework without rebranding it. Parameters: Name Type Description Default hook HookName Which hook threw — before_each or after_each . required cause BaseException The integrator's original exception, preserved verbatim. required
docs.title: ExternalIntegrationFailure

Every to_json in the taxonomy is wrapped at class creation, so a subclass need not know the masking exists.

docs.text: Measurement ( name : str , value : int | float | None , unit : str | None , limits : Limits | None , in_limits : bool | None , timestamp : datetime , ) One utils.measure call, exactly as recorded. Frozen because the record is sealed with the node: a consumer keys a time series on name together with the node path, so a value that could change after the call would corrupt the series it belongs to. in_limits is None when the reading was recorded without a window, True or False otherwise; it is a recorded fact, and the verdict is decided elsewhere. A reading that was not taken has value=None . It is never inside its window, so in_limits is False when limits were given: a gate written on the window fails the claim however it is spelled, and the claim decides what a missing reading means. Without limits it is None , as for any trend reading. Attributes: Name Type Description name str The identity of the quantity, unique within the node. value int | float | None The reading, an int or a finite float ; None when the suite tried to take it and could not. unit str | None The developer's label for the reading, or None for a dimensionless count. Never validated, never converted. limits Limits | None The inclusive (low, high) window, or None when none was given. in_limits bool | None Whether value sits inside limits ; False for a reading not taken against a window; None without limits. timestamp datetime When the reading was recorded, timezone-aware UTC.
docs.title: Measurement

The node rendered no verdict, and the framework will not forge Fail or Pass on its behalf. Renders node-local Aborted; siblings are unaffected, because one author's missing return must not take down a seventy-DUT run. Record the non-verdict a node returned. docs.text: Bases: StrEnum The six survey dispatch points of one node lifecycle, in the order they occur. The values are the artifact-name prefixes the Evidence Contract already publishes ( pre-configure-1 ), so naming a phase in code names it in the run directory. Members order by declaration, not by string: Phase.PRE_TEST < Phase.POST_TEST holds. Order is not reach. After a failed configure the engine skips post-configure, pre-test, and post-test and still fires pre-cleanup and post-cleanup, so a survey scheduled "post-configure onward" guards the device with utils.exec_route , not with the phase.
docs.title: Phase

docs.text: RunEnv ( values : Mapping [ str , str ]) Bases: Mapping [ str , str ] The run environment: a read-only mapping with readers that Fail the run. Contract It is the filtered, immutable snapshot TestUtils.env publishes on every RunResult . get , in , [] , and iteration behave as on any mapping. text(name) trims the value and treats blank as unset. A bench script that exports TARGET_PASSWORD="" means "no password", not "the empty password". require(name) raises TestFailure naming the variable to set. Called from configure , that is the "did not reach a testable state" verdict: the run Fails before any claim runs, and the message is the operator's instruction. port(name, default=22) parses an integer in 1-65535 and raises TestFailure for anything else, so a bench typo is reported as the variable rather than surfacing later as a transport error. int(name, default=) and float(name, default=) do the same for a number. Unset or blank uses default when one was passed, and otherwise Fails naming the variable. A value that is not a base-10 integer, or not a finite float, Fails naming the variable and the value.
docs.title: RunEnv

docs.text: Bases: StrEnum The three terminal states. Peers — Aborted is not a flavor of failure. There is no fourth. A call that settles without producing a terminal state (a successful configure , a completed cleanup ) reports Outcome.state is None , which says "nothing terminal happened here" rather than inventing a state to say it.
docs.title: State

docs.text: SummaryTreeNode ( name : str , type : NodeType , state : State | None , failure : Failure | None = None , timeout : TimeoutEvidence | None = None , log_path : str | None = None , children : tuple [ SummaryTreeNode , ... ] = (), evidence : JsonObject | None = None , evidence_declared : tuple [ str , ... ] | None = None , measurements : tuple [ JsonObject , ... ] | None = None , ) Plain recursive snapshot consumed by a future Inspector. state is None means the node was declared but did not run, as can happen to later steps in a failed sequence. It is not a fourth terminal state. log_path links this node to its persisted timeline. It is the POSIX path of the node's timeline.jsonl relative to the run directory, so a copied run directory keeps every link intact. It is None for a node that never ran and for a node whose records rolled up into an ancestor; an Inspector resolves the latter by walking to the nearest ancestor that carries a path. evidence is what a leaf's verdict carried, PASS(evidence) or TestFailure(..., evidence=...) , already validated and detached. evidence_declared is the leaf's @evidence declaration. A declared key absent from evidence is a reading that was not taken; an Inspector shows it by name. Both are None on a node that is not a leaf, that never ran, or that declared nothing (issue #118). measurements is every utils.measure call this node recorded, in call order, as version-1 measurement objects. It sits on the tree node rather than only in the node's own run_data because result.json is the root's record: a leaf's run_data never reaches the file the Floor Technician and the SPC consumer open (issue #86). An empty tuple means the node ran and measured nothing; None means the node never ran, matching state .
docs.title: SummaryTreeNode

docs.text: TestComponent ( * , name : str , discrete_log_file : bool = True , fail_after : float | None = None , abort_after : float | None = None ) A claim about hardware and the procedure that produces its evidence. Instances accept configuration during construction and are immutable afterwards. Calling :meth: main consumes the instance: a second call raises :class: ContractViolation , preserving the first run as evidence. CtxT is opt-in sugar (issue #75): a suite that narrows configure 's return to a local TypedDict and declares class MySuite(TestComponent[MyCtx]) gets utils: TestUtils[MyCtx] in configure , cleanup , and any test method that asks for it. Composition and internal plumbing (sequence/parallel children, the leaf/sequence/parallel specializations) hold TestComponent[Any] instead of the bare, defaulted alias: they compose nodes of any CtxT and must not force every child onto one suite's context shape. Create a named, not-yet-run test node. Parameters: Name Type Description Default name str Stable node name used by logs, artifacts, and failures. required discrete_log_file bool Own a per-node timeline. Set false only when this composed node should roll its records into its parent. True fail_after float | None Positive finite seconds before this subtree renders Fail. None abort_after float | None Positive finite seconds before this subtree renders Aborted. None
docs.title: TestComponent

docs.text: redact_ctx : Sequence [ str | Pattern [ str ]] = () Ctx keys whose values are not for the record (issue #154). Each entry names a key configure() returns, exactly or as a regular expression that the key matches whole; a compiled pattern is taken as written. A subclass adds to its bases' entries and never replaces them. The claims read the real value from utils.ctx as usual; the record does not carry it. run_data shows the key with the value <REDACTED> , and a string under a redacted key is masked wherever it appears: the scoped log, a failure's message and comparison, evidence on a verdict, RunResult.to_json() , and every file in the run directory. This is the same standard the framework holds an SSH credential to ( docs/contracts.md , Evidence Contract). An invalid declaration is a TypeError at class definition.
docs.title: redact_ctx

A leaf's RunResult.run_data is this view plus the evidence its verdict carried; the merge happens when the leaf settles, so an override here sees only the context (issue #118). A key the suite's redact_ctx claims appears as <REDACTED> (issue #154).

docs.text: test ( name : str , fn : _TestFunction , / , * args : object , fail_after : float | None = None , abort_after : float | None = None , ** kwargs : object , ) -> TestComponent [ Any ] Create the leaf node: a name, a verdict method, and that method's arguments. The framework calls fn(utils, *args, **kwargs) . A suite stamps out one leaf per core, rail, or channel from a single method by naming each leaf and passing the value that varies. fail_after and abort_after are the leaf's budget and never reach fn ; a test method cannot take parameters of those names. The arguments are checked against fn 's signature here, at composition time, so a leaf that could never be called fails build_suite before any hardware is touched. Static checkers cannot see through this call (PEP 612 forbids keyword parameters between *args and **kwargs of a ParamSpec ).

docs.text: run ( * , env : Mapping [ str , str ] | None = None , env_allow : Iterable [ str ] | None = None , env_deny : Iterable [ str ] | None = None , before_each : BeforeEachHook | None = None , after_each : AfterEachHook | None = None , allow_unpaired_hooks : bool = False , fail_after : float | None = None , abort_after : float | None = None , output_budget : int = DEFAULT_EXEC_OUTPUT_BUDGET , subtree : Sequence [ int ] | None = None , suite_target : str | None = None ) -> RunResult Execute once, fanning root-owned integration hooks across every node. env_allow / env_deny select which environment variables the run publishes; see TestUtils for the contract. Raises ValueError when both are given. output_budget is the combined stdout+stderr ceiling for every exec this run issues, local or SSH. subtree confines execution to one declared node: child positions from the root, so (0, 1) is the second child of the root's suite. Every node on the path to it still runs its own configure and cleanup, because that is their lifecycle and the only way the selected node meets the hop its ancestors own; every leaf outside the subtree is left pending, never executed. This is what the Inspector's Re-Run tab calls (Ty's ruling of 2026-09-10, docs/inspector.md ); it is not ancestor-configure replay, which stays prohibited. A position the declared tree does not have raises ContractViolation before anything runs. suite_target is recorded in result.json as the loader target that produced the run ( path.py::SuiteClass ), so hilt inspect can offer the same suite for re-running without deriving one from evidence. hilt run supplies it; a run started from a developer's own harness may leave it unset.
docs.title: run

docs.text: TestFailure ( fail_message : str , expected : object = MISSING , received : object = MISSING , * , evidence : Mapping [ str , object ] | None = None ) Bases: HiltError A verdict of Fail: the hardware did not meet the spec. Raised by suite code. Caught and recorded at the child boundary, which is what makes a failing DUT data rather than control flow — server 12 failing POST does not disturb the other 69. Raised from configure() it means "did not reach a testable state". Whether the cause was hardware or infrastructure is not knowable from code; the human triager decides and the framework does not pretend otherwise. Record what failed and, when given, the comparison that proves it. Parameters: Name Type Description Default fail_message str What failed, in the FT's language. required expected object The spec-defined value, when there is one. MISSING received object The value actually observed — unknown, which is why we test. MISSING evidence Mapping [ str , object ] | None Readings taken before the failure, carried into the leaf's run_data beside the verdict. A failure is not held to the method's @evidence declaration; it records whatever it is handed. None
docs.title: TestFailure

docs.text: has_comparison : bool True if this failure carries structured expected/received values. Check before rendering the comparison, so a failure that is self-evident does not print two empty columns.
docs.title: has_comparison

docs.text: is_bug : bool True if this Fail was caused by broken code rather than broken hardware.
docs.title: is_bug

docs.text: TestUtils ( * , ctx : dict [ str , Any ] | None = None , env : Mapping [ str , str ] | None = None , env_allow : Iterable [ str ] | None = None , env_deny : Iterable [ str ] | None = None , logger : Logger | None = None , artifact_root : str | Path | None = None , output_budget : int = DEFAULT_EXEC_OUTPUT_BUDGET , _integration_hooks : IntegrationHooks | None = None , _runtime : NodeRuntime | None = None , _suite_target : str | None = None ) The single fully scoped service object passed to every lifecycle method. A node owns the object, logger, and routing policy. Its authored composition receives distinct TestUtils objects which deliberately share that authored instance's mutable ctx . A composed TestComponent subclass instead begins with a fresh context, preserving instance locality. CtxT is opt-in sugar (issue #75): the runtime object is always a :class: RunContext , a framework-owned dict[str, Any] . A suite that narrows configure 's return to a local TypedDict and declares class MySuite(TestComponent[MyCtx]) gets that type back from :attr: ctx in every method it types as utils: TestUtils[MyCtx] — pyright then catches a typo in a ctx key at the call site. Nothing forces a suite to parameterize; the default Mapping[str, Any] reproduces today's un-parameterized behavior exactly. Everything the lifecycle drives lives on the :class: NodeRuntime this object holds; the methods here are the author's reads and writes of that same state. Create an unscoped run seed; lifecycle execution creates node views. Raises ValueError when both env_allow and env_deny are given. Parameters: Name Type Description Default ctx dict [ str , Any ] | None Initial root context, copied into the run's context; read it back through :attr: ctx . The framework mutates that copy in place. None env Mapping [ str , str ] | None Environment source. Defaults to the process environment. The published snapshot is an immutable copy, filtered per the lists below. None env_allow Iterable [ str ] | None Regular expressions; only variables whose name matches one ( re.search ) are published. Exclusive with env_deny . None env_deny Iterable [ str ] | None Regular expressions; variables whose name matches one are withheld. Exclusive with env_allow . With either list, environment=DEBUG in the source publishes every variable and logs a warning saying so. None logger Logger | None Logging sink beneath the per-node scope adapter. None artifact_root str | Path | None Directory for point-in-time evidence. Defaults to the HILT_ARTIFACT_ROOT environment snapshot, then ./artifacts . None output_budget int Combined stdout+stderr ceiling in bytes for every exec this run issues, local or SSH. Defaults to DEFAULT_EXEC_OUTPUT_BUDGET (4 MiB). DEFAULT_EXEC_OUTPUT_BUDGET
docs.title: TestUtils

Beyond the mapping, RunEnv.require , text , and port read a bench variable and Fail the run naming it when it is missing or malformed.
