docs.text: exec_route : str The host utils.exec lands on right now: "local" or the hop's endpoint. "local" is the test host, before any use_shell and after use_shell(inherit=False) . Otherwise it is the endpoint of the hop this node's route attaches to, the last name in the exec routing: evidence line ( "10.10.10.10" for a route bastion -> 10.10.10.10 ). A survey reads this to know whether there is a device on the other end of exec at the phase it fires, which the phase alone cannot say.
docs.title: exec_route

docs.text: capture_artifact ( artifact : Artifact ) -> Path Persist evidence and append its structured pointer to the scoped timeline. The file is durably published before the pointer is logged. Serialization or persistence failures therefore produce neither a misleading pointer nor a partially published artifact.
docs.title: capture_artifact

docs.text: exec ( command : str ) -> ExecResult Run command through this node's active route. Never raises for the command's own exit status. A non-zero exit_code is evidence for the test method to judge, not an exception. Signal-killed and aborted commands settle as exit_code == -1 . A closed transport (including after cancel_in_flight ) settles the same way, with the protocol error on stderr — RemoteInterface.exec still raises ConnectionError internally; this method is the author-facing surface and stays total. Hitting the output budget terminates the command and settles with truncated=True ; that is evidence, not an exception. CancelledError still propagates: that is TaskGroup teardown, not a command outcome.
docs.title: exec

docs.text: wait_for ( predicate : Callable [[], Awaitable [ T ]], * , looking_for : str , interval : float = ... , timeout_seconds : float = ... ) -> T wait_for ( predicate : Callable [[], T ], * , looking_for : str , interval : float = ... , timeout_seconds : float = ... ) -> T wait_for ( predicate : WaitPredicate [ T ], * , looking_for : str , interval : float = 1.0 , timeout_seconds : float = 30.0 ) -> T Poll until predicate returns a truthy value, and hand that value back. A predicate that returns True still yields True . Any other truthy value — the entries a query log just found, a parsed reading — is what the caller receives, so the observation does not have to live in a closure (issue #158). Falsy results keep polling. A timeout raises TestFailure with looking_for as the expected value and "timeout" as the received one. Parameters: Name Type Description Default predicate WaitPredicate [ T ] Sync or async callable, polled until it returns a truthy value. required looking_for str Plain-language name of the condition. It is the Floor Technician's primary diagnostic when the wait times out. required interval float Seconds between polls. Must be greater than zero. 1.0 timeout_seconds float Seconds to keep polling. Zero polls once, then times out if that look was falsy. 30.0 Returns: Type Description T The predicate's last truthy value. Raises: Type Description TestFailure The window closed before a truthy value. ValueError interval is not positive, or timeout_seconds is negative.
docs.title: wait_for

docs.text: get_arp_resolver ( * , mac : str , ping_count : int = 1 ) -> ArpResolver Return a MAC-to-IP resolver scoped to this node's current exec route. ARP table reads and pings go through utils.exec , so they land on the same host as the rest of this node's commands — local, or through a via hop. The routing label is the cache key: devices behind different gateways keep independent ARP state. Parameters: Name Type Description Default mac str Device MAC in any usual form (colons, dashes, or bare hex). required ping_count int ICMP packets per ping() . Defaults to 1. 1
docs.title: get_arp_resolver

docs.text: use_shell ( * , host : str | None = None , username : str | None = None , port : int = 22 , password : str | None = None , private_key : str | bytes | None = None , private_key_path : str | Path | None = None , passphrase : str | None = None , agent : str | None = None , skip_host_verification : bool = False , via : Shell | None = None , inherit : bool = True , propagate : bool = True ) -> Shell Declare this node's exec route from configure() , or read the active one. With no arguments this returns the active Shell and may be called from any slot. A route-shaping argument ( host , via , inherit=False , propagate=False ) declares the route, and the framework admits that only while this node's configure() is running: the exec routing: line is written when configure returns and the FT reads it as true for the whole node (Exec Routing Contract). From any other slot the declaring call raises ContractViolation before the router is touched.

docs.text: use_serial ( * , device : str | None = None , baud : int = 115200 , prompt : str | None = None , login_prompt : str | None = None , password_prompt : str | None = None , username : str | None = None , password : str | None = None , login_timeout : float = 10.0 , prompt_timeout : float = 30.0 , bridge_command : str | None = None , output_budget : int | None = None , via : Shell | None = None , inherit : bool = True , propagate : bool = True ) -> Shell Declare this node's exec route through a console from configure() , or read it. use_serial(device=...) is use_shell(host=...) for a console reached by its device path ( /dev/ttyUSB0 ): the port is opened, utils.exec is bound to it for this node and its descendants, and the framework closes it after the post-cleanup survey and on abort. With no arguments this returns the active Shell and may be called from any slot. The declaring form is admitted only while this node's configure() is running, for the reason use_shell gives: the exec routing: line is written when configure returns and the FT reads it as true for the whole node (Exec Routing Contract). From any other slot the declaring call raises ContractViolation before the router is touched. Parameters: Name Type Description Default device str | None The device node, on the test host or, with via or an inherited SSH route, on the hop box. None baud int Line rate requested at open. 115200 prompt str | None Regex matched against the tail of decoded output; None is a bare POSIX prompt. Supply it for anything else — a prompt guessed at runtime is how a stuck read gets misread as a fast command. None login_prompt str | None Regex answered with username during connect, if the console logs in. None password_prompt str | None Regex answered with password during connect. None username str | None Login name; required when login_prompt is given. None password str | None Login secret. Never rendered in evidence. None login_timeout float Seconds to resolve login and the first prompt at connect. 10.0 prompt_timeout float Seconds one exec waits for the prompt before settling exit_code == -1 with the text so far as evidence. 30.0 bridge_command str | None Remote command whose stdin/stdout is the UART, for a console behind a hop. Defaults to a stty + cat bridge. None output_budget int | None Per-exec output ceiling for this console; None is the run's shared ceiling. None via Shell | None An SSH Shell to bridge through. A serial console accepts no other kind of hop. None inherit bool Bridge through an inherited SSH route when via is omitted. True propagate bool False keeps this route from flowing to children. True
docs.title: use_serial

None token str | None Optional Bearer token. Named as a path in logs, never the value. None verify bool TLS verification. False is lab-only and logged as such. docs.text: measure ( name : str , value : int | float | None , * , unit : str | None = None , limits : Limits | None = None ) -> Measurement Record one parametric reading on this node, beside the verdict. A limit is evidence, never a verdict: the reading is recorded with in_limits decided and nothing about the node's state changes. When the window is a pass criterion, gate on the returned record in plain sight so the verdict's predicate is visible to the reader and to hilt/gated-pass :: rail = utils.measure("output_voltage_v", volts, unit="V", limits=(4.75, 5.25)) if rail.in_limits: return PASS({"output_voltage_v": volts}) raise TestFailure("rail outside window", "4.75-5.25 V", f"{volts} V") A reading the suite could not take is value=None , recorded as not taken (issue #159). It is never inside its window, so the gate above fails the claim on a missing reading without a try around every read over a shell; without a window it is a trend entry with a hole, and the verdict stays where the claim put it. Synchronous and free of I/O, so no cancellation can land between the reading and its record. Allowed from configure() and the test method only, the two slots that produce the node's record; the record is sealed when the node settles. hilt.measure is the same call resolved to the running node. Parameters: Name Type Description Default name str Non-empty identity of the quantity, unique within this node. For the life of the suite it names the same quantity in the same unit; a consumer keys its series on it. required value int | float | None An int or finite float , or None when the reading could not be taken. A textual observation is evidence on the verdict, not a measurement; NaN is a bug in the suite, not a missing reading. required unit str | None Free label such as "V" or "ms" , or None for a dimensionless count. Never validated, never converted. None limits Limits | None Inclusive (low, high) window with None on an open side, or None to record for trend with in_limits unset. None Returns: Type Description Measurement The frozen Measurement exactly as recorded. Raises: Type Description ContractViolation When an argument is refused, when the name was already recorded in this node, or when the call comes from outside configure() or the test method.
docs.title: measure

docs.text: The value that means "this node passed", with or without evidence. Contract Exactly one bare instance exists per interpreter. Verdict() returns it; copying, deep-copying, and unpickling all return it. It is the value bound to PASS . PASS(evidence) mints a verdict that carries a detached copy of evidence . It is a distinct object, so identity with PASS is never the check: the child boundary asks isinstance(result, Verdict) . evidence is read-only. The boundary copies it into run_data after checking every entry; a carrying verdict cannot be edited after it is returned. repr() is the bare word PASS , or PASS({...}) for a carrying verdict, so logs and artifacts read as the FT expects rather than showing an address. The type parameter is the evidence shape. A method annotated -> Verdict[MyEvidence] with a TypedDict has its PASS({...}) payload checked against that shape by pyright; the bare -> Verdict accepts any mapping.

docs.text: evidence : Mapping [ str , object ] | None The readings this verdict carries, or None for the bare PASS .

docs.text: @evidence : the readings a test method promises to carry on PASS . A test method is a function from utils.ctx to a verdict. The decorator is the method's return signature: it names the keys a pass must carry, beside the code that keeps the promise. It annotates and registers nothing; build_suite still names and binds the method. The declaration is fixed at class definition and never computed at run time: pass criteria that vary by SKU or fixture are a leaf argument or a different leaf, decided before build_suite runs (issue #118). The child boundary holds PASS to the declaration: a declared key the payload does not carry is a ContractViolation naming the leaf and the key. Extra keys are allowed; the declaration is a floor. TestFailure is not held to it, since a failure may fire before every reading was taken. An undecorated method may still return PASS(payload) ; the payload is recorded unchecked. Two spellings:: @evidence("output_voltage_v") async def _check_voltage(self, utils: TestUtils) -> Verdict: ... class VoltageEvidence(TypedDict): output_voltage_v: float @evidence(VoltageEvidence) async def _check_voltage(self, utils: TestUtils) -> Verdict[VoltageEvidence]: ... The TypedDict form declares its required keys at run time and lets pyright check the PASS({...}) payload against the shape at write time.

Parameters: Name Type Description Default *keys str | type [ Mapping [ str , object ]] String keys, or exactly one TypedDict class whose required keys are the declaration. () Raises: Type Description TypeError The declaration is empty, mixes the two spellings, repeats a key, or names a class that is not a TypedDict .

docs.text: measure ( name : str , value : int | float | None , * , unit : str | None = None , limits : Limits | None = None ) -> Measurement Record a measurement on the node whose configure() or test method is running. The package-root spelling of utils.measure (issue #85, Ty's condition): the same signature, the same rules, the same record. It exists so from hilt import measure reads naturally in a suite; utils.measure remains the documented home. Outside a running slot there is no node to record against, so the call is refused rather than recorded somewhere surprising. Parameters: Name Type Description Default name str Non-empty identity of the quantity, unique within the node. required value int | float | None An int or finite float , or None for a reading not taken. required unit str | None Free label such as "V" or "ms" , or None for a count. None limits Limits | None Inclusive (low, high) window, None on an open side, or None . None Returns: Type Description Measurement The frozen Measurement , with in_limits already decided. Raises: Type Description MeasurementUnbound When no node's configure() or test method is executing in the current task.

docs.text: Developer-Framework Contracts ¶ The contracts below define the mutual obligations between the developer and the framework. These are non-negotiable invariants. Any API change must preserve every contract listed here. In the Python port, tier-1 enforcement of these contracts lives in the child-boundary wrapper ( src/hilt/lifecycle.py , ChildBoundary ): every call the framework makes into suite code passes through it, and per-slot policy ( SLOT_POLICIES ) is declared once and read nowhere else. Nothing that protects hardware or verdict integrity may live only in static analysis. Lifecycle Contract ¶ Developer obligation: Implement configure() , build_suite() , and cleanup() with the correct intent. - configure() — put the test in a known state and return what the tests will read. Readiness gates and polling live here. The return is a plain dict (or a local TypedDict under pyright strict; the framework annotation is Mapping[str, Any] ) whose entries become utils.ctx for test methods, hooks, cleanup() , and all descendant tests. Ctx does not change after that: a [] read of a key configure() did not provide, and any write once it has returned, is a ContractViolation naming the test and the key, not a hardware Fail. .get() and in read an optional key (issues #112, #118). - build_suite() — pure table-of-contents composition. Return a TestComponent built from self.test() / self.sequence() / self.parallel() . Test methods (private class methods passed to self.test() ) carry the actual verdict logic — return PASS , or PASS(evidence) with the readings, to pass; raise TestFailure (optionally with evidence= ) to fail intentionally. - cleanup() — restore state. Must not throw (errors are swallowed and logged). It reads ctx and does not write it; a value it must restore was captured in configure() . Framework obligation: Execute configure → build_suite → cleanup in order, guaranteed. - If configure() raises a TestFailure : cleanup runs, test methods never run, the test lands in Fail . The verdict means "the device did not reach a testable state" — whether the underlying cause is hardware or infrastructure is not knowable from code and is the human triager's call. - If configure() raises anything else: wrapped as a ContractViolation ("CONTRACT VIOLATION IN : ... escaped the node", recorded as Fail with bug: true ) — configure must signal verdicts via TestFailure . - If a test method raises a plain exception: wrapped as a ContractViolation the same way — a developer contract violation, not a hardware failure. - A cancellation already delivered to suite code outranks any return value or different exception produced after a pathological catch. The child boundary restores the cancellation before classifying that settlement, so an aborted run cannot forge a hardware or bug verdict. - cleanup() always runs regardless of any prior outcome — after configure failure and after abort. Framework finalization shields it from caller cancellation within its own bounded timeout; repeated cancellation cannot abandon that wait, and the original cancellation is re-raised after cleanup settles or exhausts the evidence budget. - The evidence budget is 30 seconds, granted per node , not per run. Each node's cleanup draws its own allowance, so a deep tree tearing down after an abort can spend up to N × 30 seconds before the abort reaches the operator — plan teardown depth with that ceiling in mind. A cleanup that exhausts its allowance is a ContractViolation charged to that node. - Lifecycle execution order is enforced at runtime by the child boundary — the type system is not the enforcer. Terminal State Contract ¶ Framework obligation: Every run of a TestComponent resolves to exactly one of three peer terminal states. The states are distinct categories with distinct recovery protocols — the framework does not collapse them. There is no hidden fourth: a call that settles without producing a terminal state (a successful configure , a completed cleanup ) reports no state at all rather than inventing one. Pass — a test method returned a Verdict : the bare PASS , or PASS(evidence) carrying its readings. The check is isinstance(result, Verdict) ; a Verdict is obtained only by importing PASS or calling it, so nothing a suite constructs can forge one. A pass without its declared evidence is not a pass: when the method carries @evidence(...) , a PASS that does not carry every declared key is a ContractViolation (developer-bug Fail), never a green run (issue #118). Fail — a test method raised a TestFailure (or subclass): the DUT produced a verdict and the verdict was negative. OR the developer didn't model a failure mode: a plain exception → ContractViolation Fail ( bug: true ). Aborted — no verdict was produced. Peer to Pass/Fail, NOT a flavor of failure. Three causes: Harness-level (integration): a before_each / after_each integration hook threw; the error is wrapped as ExternalIntegrationFailure and the run halts before a verdict could be produced. Harness-level (operator): SIGINT or SIGTERM arrived while a run was live; the failure is OperatorInterrupt so the Floor Technician reads that the operator stopped the rack. The same run-abort path fires as a hook throw: Aborted everywhere, transports hard-closed, RunResult returned. Node-local: a test method returned anything other than the PASS sentinel — None fall-through or an explicit wrong value ( MissingVerdict ). No verdict exists, so the framework refuses to forge Fail (or Pass) on its behalf. Siblings are unaffected. (Deliberate deviation from the TypeScript original, which folded this into the contract-violation/Fail path.) Developer obligation: Recognize the taxonomy. A TestFailure means "the DUT failed a check"; an ExternalIntegrationFailure means "the harness around the test broke"; an OperatorInterrupt means "the operator stopped the rack." Never conflate them — the Floor Technician's recovery protocol depends on knowing which. A KeyboardInterrupt raised from suite code is not an operator signal: the child boundary still passes it through unrecorded. Framework obligation: When a descendant's hook throws, the ExternalIntegrationFailure propagates up through every ancestor class-intact. Sequences and parallel nodes do not rewrap it. Every ancestor's state cascades to Aborted. Time Budget Contract ¶ Framework obligation: Any node may declare a time budget by naming the terminal state it produces on expiry: fail_after= (seconds) or abort_after= (seconds). Exactly one name, or neither. Both on one node is a ContractViolation at composition time. A node with neither has no deadline of its own and is bounded only by its ancestors. Durations must be positive, finite numbers; booleans, zero, negatives, infinities, NaN, and non-numbers are rejected before execution. The pair is part of the TestComponent fractal atom. It is accepted by authored-node construction, self.test() , self.parallel() , self.sequence() , and root run() . Every node is a suite, so every placement reads the same way: this suite completes within the budget or the named state is raised. Construction and run() are two ways to declare the root's one budget, not a way to attach two clocks to one node. The window opens when the node enters configure and closes when its test method, or its last child, settles. Leaves, parallel nodes, and sequences open the equivalent window at their test/child boundary. Cleanup runs after the cut on its own finalization budget. Root-owned before_each and after_each integration hooks are outside every declared node window; time spent in them cannot spend an ancestor's hardware-verdict budget. A budget bounds the whole subtree. Every declared clock remains active while its subtree does test work. Descendants inherit all ancestor bounds and may only tighten them. The clock that fires first decides the state; a descendant's longer declaration can never loosen an ancestor's remaining time. A wait_for timeout longer than the effective enclosing budget never fires—the budget wins. Concurrent descendants are separate active lineages: one sibling entering an excluded hook or cleanup cannot pause an ancestor clock while another sibling is still doing timed work. The clock stalls only while no descendant lineage is inside its timed window. Expiry settles every descendant still running with the winning clock's declared state. fail_after renders Fail with a structured TestFailure naming the budget. abort_after renders node-local Aborted without forging a failure verdict. Descendants already settled retain their verdicts, and a composite follows the ordinary terminal aggregation rule: any Aborted outranks Fail. Deadline Aborted is node-local. It never fires the shared run halt and never cascades beyond the bounded subtree. Siblings outside that subtree are untouched under the Group Isolation Contract. Expiry is never classified as a BUG. Expiry cancels the coroutine and hard-cancels at the resource every transport the cut node itself opened. An inherited route is never in that owned set and is not touched; it remains the parent's, available to the parent and to every sibling behind it. A parent whose configure() opens the hop owns its own configure window. If that window expires, the Fail or Aborted state and its timeout evidence are the parent's, and the children it never composed render as the Lifecycle Contract says for a parent that never reached a testable state. Every cut node carries structured timeout evidence with reason="timeout" , the declared name, the declared budget in seconds, active elapsed seconds, and the root-to-node path of the clock that fired. This evidence appears on RunResult , in every affected summary_tree node, and in their JSON forms. Developer obligation: Choose the name for what “took too long” means at that step. fail_after says the hardware did not do its job in time; abort_after says the harness gave up and no verdict exists. Never swallow asyncio.CancelledError ; doing so would obstruct every deadline declared above the await. Consequence: Fail at a deadline sends the Floor Technician to the hardware. Aborted at a deadline sends them to the harness. The composition names that distinction, and the record identifies the exact clock and budget without requiring the suite source. Failure Taxonomy Contract ¶ Framework obligation: Every failure must be traceable to one of the following root causes, made obvious by signal: 1. DUT failed a check — TestFailure from a test method or from configure() . State = Fail. A TestFailure from configure() carries an extra ambiguity: the device did not reach a testable state, but whether the cause is hardware or infrastructure cannot be determined from code. The framework surfaces the looking_for / failure message; the human triager decides. 2. Hardware lying — survey artifacts expose mismatch between claimed and actual state. 3. Test method bug — a plain exception from a test method or from configure() → all failure modes modeled by the developer must raise TestFailure . Anything else raised is a bug. Full stop. A missing verdict (non-PASS return) is likewise a contract violation, rendered as node-local Aborted because no verdict exists to report. 4. External integration failure — ExternalIntegrationFailure from a before_each / after_each hook. State = Aborted. 5. Operator interrupt — OperatorInterrupt from SIGINT/SIGTERM during a live run() . State = Aborted. The failure names the operator and the signal. Developer obligation: Use the right signal for the right category. - Raise TestFailure for any verdict — from a test method or from configure() — never a plain exception. - Use survey hooks to capture device-reported state at phase boundaries. - Use configure() for environment/readiness gating. A timeout there is a TestFailure whose cause (hardware vs. infrastructure) is for the human to determine — the framework will not pretend to know. - Let the framework raise ExternalIntegrationFailure — developers do not construct or raise it directly. It is raised automatically when a before_each / after_each hook throws anything. Evidence Contract ¶ Framework obligation: Every run produces scoped, structured evidence automatically. - Logging is scoped to the current leaf test. - Survey and audit hooks share the same automatic artifact contract: every non- None return is faithfully recorded as an Artifact, including empty dicts, lists, and strings. Python resolves an explicit return None , a delegated call that returns None , and a fall-through to the same runtime value, so None writes only an informational log entry and no automatic artifact. When None itself is meaningful evidence, the SE must make that intent explicit with await utils.capture_artifact(Artifact(..., data=None)) inside the hook. - Once a hook returns a non- None observation, its automatic artifact publication is shielded from shutdown within its own 30-second evidence budget. Repeated cancellation cannot orphan an accepted observation after the hardware was read. - Survey dispatch points are the six members of Phase , in order: pre-configure , post-configure , pre-test , post-test , pre-cleanup , and post-cleanup , limited to the phases the lifecycle reaches. The artifact name identifies the dispatch point and registered-hook index; audit names identify both the hook and interval dispatch. Both use artifact type survey , keeping one Inspector evidence contract. - use_survey(fn, phases=...) schedules a survey at a subset of those points; the default is all six, and an empty selection is a ValueError at registration. A boundary the survey is not scheduled at writes one debug line and no artifact, so the run directory holds one artifact per boundary the survey was meant to observe. - Order is not reach. The phases are totally ordered, but after a failed configure the engine skips post-configure , pre-test , and post-test and still fires pre-cleanup and post-cleanup , with utils.exec on the test host if use_shell never returned. A survey that reads the device therefore guards on utils.exec_route , not on the phase; the phase says when, the route says where. - Log artifacts are co-located with their node. - Evidence travels with the verdict (issue #118). A leaf's readings leave its test method as PASS(evidence) or TestFailure(..., evidence=...) . The child boundary validates the payload entry by entry before it is recorded: a value that is not JSON, a key that shadows a ctx entry or the framework-owned measurements slot, or a key @evidence declared that PASS did not carry is a ContractViolation naming the leaf and the key. Nothing is stripped silently. A failure is not held to the declaration; it records what it was handed. - A leaf's RunResult.run_data is the JSON-safe view of its ctx plus the evidence its verdict carried, flat. A non-leaf node's run_data is the ctx view alone. Every summary_tree node carries evidence (what the leaf's verdict carried, or null) and evidence_declared (the @evidence declaration, or null); a declared key absent from evidence is a reading that was not taken, shown by name. - All serializable values (primitives, plain dicts, lists) configure() returned appear in run_data , except under a key the suite's redact_ctx claims (issue #154): that key appears with the value <REDACTED> , whatever it holds. The claims read the real value from utils.ctx ; the record does not carry it. - Functions, class instances, and live handles (e.g. SSH connections) are stripped from the ctx view; they are the objects a run works through, not evidence. - Context annotations do not bypass this filter. A TypedDict is an ordinary dict at runtime, and each value still has to satisfy the same serialization rules. - Filtering is all-or-nothing for each top-level ctx entry. A nested instance, handle, function, cycle, non-string mapping key, or non-finite float strips that complete entry; the framework never emits partial evidence or silently coerces it. - run_data is a detached snapshot taken when the node settles. An aborted leaf contributes no evidence; readings in hand when a time budget fires are lost by design, and the scoped log and point-in-time artifacts remain for in-flight observation. - run_data["measurements"] is framework-owned: the readings utils.measure recorded on this node, in call order, written when the node settles. An authored ctx entry with that name cannot populate or replace the slot, and a run_data override cannot drop it. Aggregation, SPC, and Cpk are the consumer's, not the record's. - Measurement Contract (issue #86, docs/measurements.md ). A limit is evidence, never a verdict: utils.measure records in_limits and touches neither the node's state nor its failure. A None value is admitted as a reading not taken (issue #159): recorded with value: null , never inside its window, so a claim gated on the window fails through its own gate. The framework refuses, as a ContractViolation naming the node and the measurement: an empty name, a bool , NaN , or infinite value, a non-text unit, or a window that bounds nothing or runs backwards; the same name recorded twice in one node; a call from outside configure() or the test method ( cleanup , surveys, audits, hooks, or after the node settled); and hilt.measure where no node's slot is executing. The record is sealed on every terminal state, Aborted included, and published on the node's run_data and on every summary_tree node ( null when the node never ran). A measurement does not satisfy an @evidence declaration. - Every RunResult includes ancestor_names: list[str] (path from root) and bread_crumbs: str (joined for display), plus a summary_tree snapshot of the node's subtree state at completion. Downstream integrators can reconstruct the full Inspector tree from the root's RunResult alone. - TestFailure , ExternalIntegrationFailure , and OperatorInterrupt all implement to_json() . Serializing a RunResult produces clean JSON for downstream integrators without any custom serializer. - Provenance. Every executed node records one exec routing: <where> (<why>) line — where is local or via <chain> , why names the call that put it there ( declared via use_shell , inherited from parent , declared via use_shell(inherit=False) ). A node that never declared a route renders where alone. The line is emitted after configure returns, since use_shell lives there and the route is not final until it does. - Every transport the router opens records its provenance lines as it comes up. SSH renders ssh connect: <user>@<host>:<port> auth=<label> via=<chain> ; via=direct means the connection dials out from the test host itself. When host-key verification is skipped, SSH records a second line, ssh host-key verification skipped: <host>:<port> , so the Floor Technician can see that verification was off without opening the suite. - Via chains are rendered in full and test-host-first ( bastion -> edge -> dut ), never summarized to the last hop. - The credential path is named exactly — key-file(/path) , agent(/socket) , password , key , none — and the credential's value never appears. What is logged is what was dialed: the resolution order is declared once, in SshInterface._auth_choice , and both the connect options and the provenance line read it. A password, private-key bytes, and the contents of a key file never reach the scoped log, run_data , the env snapshot, RunResult.to_json() , or a failure repr. - A suite's own secret is held to the same standard (issue #154). redact_ctx on the suite class names the ctx keys that are not for the record, exactly or as regular expressions matched against the whole key; a subclass adds to its bases' entries and never replaces them. A string under a redacted key is masked as <REDACTED> wherever it appears, run-wide: every scoped-log record, including one the author writes by hand; a failure's str() , repr() , and to_json() , down its cause chain, once the child boundary has recorded it; evidence on a verdict; captured artifacts; run_data ; and therefore RunResult.to_json() and every file in the run directory. Only a string is a needle; a number or a handle under a redacted key is shown as <REDACTED> in the ctx view and nothing more. The env snapshot stays verbatim (issue #53): a secret that is also in the environment is kept off the record with env_deny . Masking begins when the value enters ctx, by any write path ( configure() 's return, []= , update , setdefault , |= ), so a value logged inside configure() before it enters ctx is the author's to keep quiet. Masking is plain substring replacement, so a very short secret (a two-character token, a numeric sid such as 200 ) also masks unrelated text that happens to contain it; that fails closed and is accepted. - Consequence: the Floor Technician reconstructs the run's topology and its auth decisions from the artifacts alone, without opening the suite source. Developer obligation: Instrument appropriately. - Use utils.logger (never print ) so evidence is captured in artifacts. - Use self.use_survey() for periodic state snapshots; use await utils.capture_artifact(artifact) for point-in-time captures. Artifact is a write-free value on the public surface: the utility method is the only framework API that persists it, and it always emits the chronological pointer after publication. - Return structured data from use_survey / use_audit hooks to capture it as an artifact. - Hand readings back with the verdict: PASS({...}) or TestFailure(..., evidence={...}) . Declare with @evidence(...) what a pass must carry, beside the method that keeps the promise. Temporal Backbone Contract ¶ Framework obligation: Every full run() creates one timestamped run directory beneath the configured artifact root before the root lifecycle begins. Point-in-time artifacts and every per-node timeline live beneath that directory, so a run's evidence is self-contained and cannot overwrite a neighboring run. Every executed node that owns a discrete log streams the same records into two files: timeline.log , the human line view, and timeline.jsonl , the versioned Inspector record. Both files are flushed after every entry; an interrupted process therefore preserves every complete entry already accepted by the logger. The JSON Lines record carries one complete object per physical line with format_version , UTC timestamp , root-to-leaf scope , level , and message . Artifact-pointer records also carry artifact_name , artifact_path , artifact_type , and artifact_timestamp . A logging node opens its files lazily on its first record and closes them when that node reaches its terminal boundary. A declared node that never executes opens nothing. Authored suites, sequences, and parallel nodes own a log by default. Leaves roll up to the nearest owning ancestor. Sequences, parallel nodes, and composed suites may opt into the same roll-up with discrete_log_file=False ; a root still owns the run log. TestComponent.log_path exposes the owning node's absolute timeline.jsonl path after execution. It remains None for pending nodes and nodes whose records roll up. Every summary_tree node carries the same link as log_path , rendered as a POSIX path relative to the run directory, so the structural record reaches the temporal record without the live objects. It is null for pending nodes and nodes whose records roll up; the nearest ancestor with a link holds their chronology. On Pass, Fail, and Aborted, root run() atomically publishes the root RunResult.to_json() as result.json at the run-directory root before returning. The root timeline's final entry points to that file; a failed publication cannot expose a partial replacement or a pointer to evidence that was not published. The persisted chronology and root result are framework-owned. Developer code continues to use only utils.logger and utils.capture_artifact() ; it never opens or edits timeline or result files. Developer obligation: Do not write directly into the run directory or depend on its timestamped directory name. Treat log_path and captured artifact paths as opaque evidence references. The private _run_lifecycle() entry point is not a full run and therefore does not create a timestamped run directory. Framework self-tests that invoke it directly may leave point-in-time artifacts at the configured base root; authored suites use run() . Audit Contract ¶ Framework obligation: When self.use_audit(interval=..., fn=...) is called in the constructor, the framework runs fn concurrently with the test methods on the specified interval. - Multiple audit hooks are supported — each runs on its own interval. - Every audit interval is validated during construction as positive and finite. An invalid registration cannot survive long enough to touch hardware. - Audit start/stop is framework-controlled, not caller-controlled: the loop begins immediately before the first test method runs and ends immediately after the last test method returns. No delayed start, no manual trigger. The lifecycle contract (test in runnable state before configure() returns) guarantees the audit's preconditions are met by start. - If the audit fn raises a TestFailure , the running test method is immediately cancelled and the test fails with the audit's failure. - Audit errors are not swallowed — unlike survey hooks, a throwing audit is a real failure. Survey and cleanup errors are swallowed to protect the hardware verdict; ExternalIntegrationFailure is exempt from swallowing everywhere — swallowing it would kill the halt signal. - Audit follows the same artifact contract as survey (see Evidence Contract above). - Cancellation is cooperative and asyncio-native. The run-level abort ( RunAbort in lifecycle.py ) fires when an integration hook aborts the run; a throwing audit cancels the in-flight test method; test-method completion stops the audit loop. Suite code must let asyncio.CancelledError propagate — swallowing it breaks the wind-down. - The read-only utils.signal combines the run-level integration halt with the nearest authored audit scope. Audit scope is inherited only by that node's composed suite: an audit failure cancels its own in-flight work and produces Fail without cancelling an independent parallel sibling. If an audit verdict and suite completion occur in the same event-loop turn, the audit verdict wins; evidence is not discarded by timing luck. - Every started descendant cancelled by an audit still seals its result and dispatches its paired after_each . An unsettled descendant carries the audit's TestFailure class-intact; a descendant already dispatching after_each retains the verdict that hook received. Audit cancellation never becomes a run-wide integration halt. - utils.exec threads cancellation to the underlying child process. When a cancellation fires, in-flight shell commands are killed (SIGTERM) immediately — no zombie processes outlive the test. Developer obligation: - Call self.use_audit() in the constructor with both interval and fn — both are required parameters. - Yield to the event loop ( await ) inside any long-running loop in a test method so cancellation can be delivered, and never suppress asyncio.CancelledError . - Use use_audit for active monitoring that can fail the test (e.g. thermal runaway, watchdog). Use use_survey for passive state snapshots at phase boundaries that never affect the verdict. - Raise TestFailure from the audit fn to fail the test. Return data to continue — it is always recorded as evidence. Integration Hook Contract ¶ Framework obligation: before_each and after_each are optional integration hooks registered at the root run() call. The framework threads them down to every executed descendant and dispatches them around every node's lifecycle. before_each fires immediately before a node's lifecycle begins. after_each fires immediately after a node's lifecycle completes, receiving the node's RunResult . Pair invariant: after_each fires EVEN IF before_each threw. An integrator writing a "started" row in before_each always gets a "finished" row in after_each — no orphan records in the external system. Throw from either hook → framework wraps as ExternalIntegrationFailure → the shared run-abort fires → every in-flight framework→user await across the tree unwinds at its own framework boundary → every in-flight transport is closed via cancel_in_flight() → enclosing node transitions to Aborted. The integrator's own error class arrives intact as the failure's cause. An operator SIGINT/SIGTERM during a live run takes this same halt path, with OperatorInterrupt as the reason. Hooks receive a deliberately narrow context ( BeforeEachContext / AfterEachContext ): node name, ancestor chain, breadcrumbs, scoped logger, env snapshot. NOT exec , get_shell , or capture_artifact . Integration hooks are for external coordination, not for exercising the hardware. Unpaired registration (only before_each or only after_each ) emits a loud warning at run start unless allow_unpaired_hooks=True is passed. The pairing enforces the started/finished symmetry. Developer obligation: Do not register before_each / after_each inside your TestComponent subclasses. These hooks are the integrator's contract with the outside world, not part of the test's own lifecycle. Use use_survey / use_audit for per-test observation; use before_each / after_each only when composing HILT into a larger harness. In-Flight Termination Contract ¶ Framework obligation: When the run-level abort fires (an integration hook throws anywhere in the tree, or the operator sends SIGINT/SIGTERM to a live run), every framework-managed transport is closed HARD immediately — not at the next polling boundary. Cancelling the coroutine is not enough; the framework cancels the RESOURCE. The operator-signal handler is installed by run() / main() only while that run is live, on the running loop, and removed on the way out so a library caller never leaks it. The first signal fires RunAbort with an OperatorInterrupt and hard-closes transports; a second signal inside the finalization window exits the process immediately. SshInterface destroys its underlying asyncssh connection, closing every open channel and failing every pending exec stream at the socket level. Recursively propagates through via chains — a jump-host tunnel and everything tunneled through it collapse together. RemoteInterface subclasses expose cancel_in_flight() for any transport type that needs aggressive close semantics. Long-running user operations (firmware flashes, long-polling requests, multi-step SSH scripts) in flight when the abort fires receive a dead resource, causing their own awaitables to fail and settle harmlessly in the event loop. Consequence: A 30-minute firmware flash in progress when before_each throws does NOT continue to mutate the hardware. This is load-bearing for manufacturing test integrity — the halt signal means "stop touching the hardware," and the framework enforces that at the transport layer. Group Isolation Contract ¶ Framework obligation: TestGroup runs its children concurrently under asyncio.TaskGroup , and the child boundary guarantees the TaskGroup semantics are correct: Fail and node-local Aborted are returned by the boundary, never raised — one child's failure cannot escape into the TaskGroup and cancel healthy siblings. Only a harness-level halt propagates, and the TaskGroup then cancelling everything is exactly right, because that is what Aborted means. Utils Contract ¶ Framework obligation: TestUtils is the single, fully-scoped utility surface passed to every lifecycle method. utils.exec never throws. It returns an ExecResult(stdout, stderr, exit_code, truncated, captured_bytes) — a non-zero exit code is data for the test method to judge, not an exception. Signal-killed, aborted, and closed-transport commands settle as exit_code=-1 . A ConnectionError from RemoteInterface.exec is absorbed here; the protocol stays loud, the author-facing surface stays total. CancelledError still propagates. Stdout and stderr together are bounded by one named output_budget (default 4 MiB), applied identically by the local executor and SshInterface . The budget is configured at the run seed ( TestComponent.run(output_budget=...) / TestUtils(output_budget=...) ) or at LocalExec / SshInterface construction — never as a process-global. Exceeding it terminates the command the same way abort does (SIGTERM the host process group; SIGTERM then close that SSH channel, session stays up) and settles with the bytes actually received, truncated=True , and captured_bytes equal to what was kept. Truncation is evidence, never an exception. The scoped log names it ( exec output truncated: captured N bytes (budget B) ). Streaming reads preserve interrupted output: decode happens only at settlement, with replacement for a cut in the middle of a UTF-8 sequence. Developer obligation: Use only utils.* inside lifecycle methods — never import framework internals directly into test logic. Exec Routing Contract ¶ Framework obligation: use_shell is the only writer of the node's exec router. get_shell may open extra endpoints and may read inherit to pick a tunnel; it never assigns the router or the propagate flag. Four use_shell shapes: connection ( host + username ), connection with explicit via , policy-only inherit=False (force local), and bare use_shell() (return the active handle). Explicit via always wins. inherit=False on a connection form skips the parent's hop. Declared in configure() , nowhere else. A declaring use_shell ( host , via , inherit=False , propagate=False ) is admitted only while this node's own configure() is running; from a test method, cleanup , a survey, an audit, or a helper they call, it raises ContractViolation before the router is touched. The exec routing: line is written when configure returns and the FT reads it as the truth for the node's whole run; a route moved later would make that line a lie for every command after the move. The bare use_shell() reads the active handle and may be called from any slot. A second declaration. configure() may declare more than once, since no command has yet run under the route being replaced: open a jump host, then route through it. The last declaration is the route; every shell opened on the way stays opened on this node and is not torn down early. Ownership. The node whose configure() opened a shell, through use_shell or get_shell , owns it. The framework closes it at that node's cleanup (after the post-cleanup survey, before the hop it tunnels through), never earlier and never from another node. Hooks and audits observe the route; they do not set it. They read utils.exec_route and exec through what configure() committed to. A survey runs at phases before configure() and after cleanup() , and an audit runs concurrently with the test method, so neither has a moment at which one route could be declared once. get_shell stays open to them: an auxiliary endpoint changes nothing the routing line states. propagate=False on use_shell stops this node's router from flowing to children; they start local. propagate on get_shell is a documented no-op. The parent owns the route. A route is owned by the node whose configure() declared it and is inherited by every node that node composes, down the tree, until a descendant declares inherit=False (or the owner declared propagate=False ). A device class never takes a routing argument: a gateway is a parent whose configure() opens the hop and whose build_suite() composes the devices behind it, and those devices are routed by being its children. The TestComponent constructor has no via= ; the only via is the tunnel argument to use_shell / get_shell , declared inside configure() by the node that owns the route (issue #137). Children inherit the route through run params ( RouterRunParams ), never through ctx. ctx is instance-local domain data, not infrastructure. Routed tunnels are borrowed; the router owns hop lifecycle. Every hop the router resolves — an explicit via= Shell or an inherited route — is already live, so the connector threads it through the transport's borrowed tunnel= channel, never the owned via= one. The opened interface must not disconnect, cancel, or collapse its hop. What a node opened is recorded on the node ( opened ), stays connected through the node's post-cleanup survey, and closes after that survey and before the hop it tunnels through — the parent's hop closes at the same point of the parent's own lifecycle, after every child is done with it (issue #115), so a survey that execs at post-cleanup reads the device, not a closed transport; a hard abort on the hop kills everything tunneled through it at the socket (In-Flight Termination Contract). A dead hop at open time is an error, not something the router silently brings up. Local exec and every SSH session this router opens share the run's output_budget (see the Utils Contract). A fat command is truncated and killed at the resource; it does not take the rest of the rack with it. A transport's address is fixed while it is live. connect(host, port) re-points an addressed transport only through a closed handle; asking a live one for a different address is refused, never silently replaced. After a flash or DHCP churn the flow is disconnect() , reacquire, connect(new_ip) . There is no self-healing: a socket the framework killed stays dead (In-Flight Termination Contract), and an unexpected drop reaches the author as a ConnectionError on the next exec , not as a quiet redial. utils.exec_route states where utils.exec lands at the moment it is read: local for the test host, otherwise the endpoint of the hop the route attaches to (the last name in the exec routing: chain). It is derived from the router, never stored, so it is right in a survey at every phase, including the pre-configure dispatch before use_shell has run and the pre-cleanup dispatch after a configure that failed before it. The router logs what it opens and where every node's exec lands (see the Evidence Contract). A transport that hides its hop hides the topology: endpoint , hop , and route_label on RemoteInterface are how a transport states its place in the chain, and provenance_lines (starting with connect_provenance ) are the lines the router records for it. Developer obligation: Declare in configure() , and only there, where this node's utils.exec lands when it should be somewhere other than the test host; a test method, survey, or audit that needs a different endpoint reads use_shell() or opens one with get_shell . Do not stuff SSH handles into ctx and expect routing to notice. Device API Contract ¶ Framework obligation: DeviceApiInterface is a contract, not an exec subclass ( HIL ruling 1 ). The guarantees live in the signed Device API design note ; this page does not restate them. DeviceRequest(..., json=value) is the JSON body convenience (issue #155): it serializes once to UTF-8 payload bytes and supplies Content-Type: application/json unless the request already declares a content type, matched case-insensitively. json=None sends JSON null; omitting json leaves the raw-payload API unchanged. Combining json with a non- None payload , even empty bytes, is a ValueError before any transfer. Non-serializable values and non-finite numbers are refused at construction. The request never mutates the caller's headers or retains its JSON object. DeviceResponse.json() decodes the returned bytes. parse(response_type="json") is the format-selecting form; response_type="yaml" uses yaml.safe_load from the optional hilt-core[yaml] extra. Unknown formats raise ValueError , a missing YAML dependency raises ImportError , and parser errors propagate without a fallback. Parsing is explicit, independent of response status and headers; it preserves body and status , makes no request, and supplies no verdict. A malformed body remains a completed transfer for the suite to judge. Body contents never enter attempt logs. A CoAP status is the dotted code ( "2.05" , a CoapCode constant). An HTTP status stays an integer (issue #156). Developer obligation: Implement DeviceApiInterface as that note specifies. Composability Contract ¶ Framework obligation: Any TestComponent or subclass thereof can be composed indefinitely in any shape the SE deems appropriate. Developer obligation: Leaves must be self-contained — declare their own readiness preconditions in configure() , not in the parent sequence.
docs.title: Contracts

docs.text: The contracts below define the mutual obligations between the developer and the framework. These are non-negotiable invariants. Any API change must preserve every contract listed here. In the Python port, tier-1 enforcement of these contracts lives in the child-boundary wrapper ( src/hilt/lifecycle.py , ChildBoundary ): every call the framework makes into suite code passes through it, and per-slot policy ( SLOT_POLICIES ) is declared once and read nowhere else. Nothing that protects hardware or verdict integrity may live only in static analysis.
docs.title: Developer-Framework Contracts

docs.text: Developer obligation: Implement configure() , build_suite() , and cleanup() with the correct intent. - configure() — put the test in a known state and return what the tests will read. Readiness gates and polling live here. The return is a plain dict (or a local TypedDict under pyright strict; the framework annotation is Mapping[str, Any] ) whose entries become utils.ctx for test methods, hooks, cleanup() , and all descendant tests. Ctx does not change after that: a [] read of a key configure() did not provide, and any write once it has returned, is a ContractViolation naming the test and the key, not a hardware Fail. .get() and in read an optional key (issues #112, #118). - build_suite() — pure table-of-contents composition. Return a TestComponent built from self.test() / self.sequence() / self.parallel() . Test methods (private class methods passed to self.test() ) carry the actual verdict logic — return PASS , or PASS(evidence) with the readings, to pass; raise TestFailure (optionally with evidence= ) to fail intentionally. - cleanup() — restore state. Must not throw (errors are swallowed and logged). It reads ctx and does not write it; a value it must restore was captured in configure() . Framework obligation: Execute configure → build_suite → cleanup in order, guaranteed. - If configure() raises a TestFailure : cleanup runs, test methods never run, the test lands in Fail . The verdict means "the device did not reach a testable state" — whether the underlying cause is hardware or infrastructure is not knowable from code and is the human triager's call. - If configure() raises anything else: wrapped as a ContractViolation ("CONTRACT VIOLATION IN : ... escaped the node", recorded as Fail with bug: true ) — configure must signal verdicts via TestFailure . - If a test method raises a plain exception: wrapped as a ContractViolation the same way — a developer contract violation, not a hardware failure. - A cancellation already delivered to suite code outranks any return value or different exception produced after a pathological catch. The child boundary restores the cancellation before classifying that settlement, so an aborted run cannot forge a hardware or bug verdict. - cleanup() always runs regardless of any prior outcome — after configure failure and after abort. Framework finalization shields it from caller cancellation within its own bounded timeout; repeated cancellation cannot abandon that wait, and the original cancellation is re-raised after cleanup settles or exhausts the evidence budget. - The evidence budget is 30 seconds, granted per node , not per run. Each node's cleanup draws its own allowance, so a deep tree tearing down after an abort can spend up to N × 30 seconds before the abort reaches the operator — plan teardown depth with that ceiling in mind. A cleanup that exhausts its allowance is a ContractViolation charged to that node. - Lifecycle execution order is enforced at runtime by the child boundary — the type system is not the enforcer.
docs.title: Lifecycle Contract

docs.text: Framework obligation: Every run of a TestComponent resolves to exactly one of three peer terminal states. The states are distinct categories with distinct recovery protocols — the framework does not collapse them. There is no hidden fourth: a call that settles without producing a terminal state (a successful configure , a completed cleanup ) reports no state at all rather than inventing one. Pass — a test method returned a Verdict : the bare PASS , or PASS(evidence) carrying its readings. The check is isinstance(result, Verdict) ; a Verdict is obtained only by importing PASS or calling it, so nothing a suite constructs can forge one. A pass without its declared evidence is not a pass: when the method carries @evidence(...) , a PASS that does not carry every declared key is a ContractViolation (developer-bug Fail), never a green run (issue #118). Fail — a test method raised a TestFailure (or subclass): the DUT produced a verdict and the verdict was negative. OR the developer didn't model a failure mode: a plain exception → ContractViolation Fail ( bug: true ). Aborted — no verdict was produced. Peer to Pass/Fail, NOT a flavor of failure. Three causes: Harness-level (integration): a before_each / after_each integration hook threw; the error is wrapped as ExternalIntegrationFailure and the run halts before a verdict could be produced. Harness-level (operator): SIGINT or SIGTERM arrived while a run was live; the failure is OperatorInterrupt so the Floor Technician reads that the operator stopped the rack. The same run-abort path fires as a hook throw: Aborted everywhere, transports hard-closed, RunResult returned. Node-local: a test method returned anything other than the PASS sentinel — None fall-through or an explicit wrong value ( MissingVerdict ). No verdict exists, so the framework refuses to forge Fail (or Pass) on its behalf. Siblings are unaffected. (Deliberate deviation from the TypeScript original, which folded this into the contract-violation/Fail path.) Developer obligation: Recognize the taxonomy. A TestFailure means "the DUT failed a check"; an ExternalIntegrationFailure means "the harness around the test broke"; an OperatorInterrupt means "the operator stopped the rack." Never conflate them — the Floor Technician's recovery protocol depends on knowing which. A KeyboardInterrupt raised from suite code is not an operator signal: the child boundary still passes it through unrecorded. Framework obligation: When a descendant's hook throws, the ExternalIntegrationFailure propagates up through every ancestor class-intact. Sequences and parallel nodes do not rewrap it. Every ancestor's state cascades to Aborted.
docs.title: Terminal State Contract

docs.text: Framework obligation: Any node may declare a time budget by naming the terminal state it produces on expiry: fail_after= (seconds) or abort_after= (seconds). Exactly one name, or neither. Both on one node is a ContractViolation at composition time. A node with neither has no deadline of its own and is bounded only by its ancestors. Durations must be positive, finite numbers; booleans, zero, negatives, infinities, NaN, and non-numbers are rejected before execution. The pair is part of the TestComponent fractal atom. It is accepted by authored-node construction, self.test() , self.parallel() , self.sequence() , and root run() . Every node is a suite, so every placement reads the same way: this suite completes within the budget or the named state is raised. Construction and run() are two ways to declare the root's one budget, not a way to attach two clocks to one node. The window opens when the node enters configure and closes when its test method, or its last child, settles. Leaves, parallel nodes, and sequences open the equivalent window at their test/child boundary. Cleanup runs after the cut on its own finalization budget. Root-owned before_each and after_each integration hooks are outside every declared node window; time spent in them cannot spend an ancestor's hardware-verdict budget. A budget bounds the whole subtree. Every declared clock remains active while its subtree does test work. Descendants inherit all ancestor bounds and may only tighten them. The clock that fires first decides the state; a descendant's longer declaration can never loosen an ancestor's remaining time. A wait_for timeout longer than the effective enclosing budget never fires—the budget wins. Concurrent descendants are separate active lineages: one sibling entering an excluded hook or cleanup cannot pause an ancestor clock while another sibling is still doing timed work. The clock stalls only while no descendant lineage is inside its timed window. Expiry settles every descendant still running with the winning clock's declared state. fail_after renders Fail with a structured TestFailure naming the budget. abort_after renders node-local Aborted without forging a failure verdict. Descendants already settled retain their verdicts, and a composite follows the ordinary terminal aggregation rule: any Aborted outranks Fail. Deadline Aborted is node-local. It never fires the shared run halt and never cascades beyond the bounded subtree. Siblings outside that subtree are untouched under the Group Isolation Contract. Expiry is never classified as a BUG. Expiry cancels the coroutine and hard-cancels at the resource every transport the cut node itself opened. An inherited route is never in that owned set and is not touched; it remains the parent's, available to the parent and to every sibling behind it. A parent whose configure() opens the hop owns its own configure window. If that window expires, the Fail or Aborted state and its timeout evidence are the parent's, and the children it never composed render as the Lifecycle Contract says for a parent that never reached a testable state. Every cut node carries structured timeout evidence with reason="timeout" , the declared name, the declared budget in seconds, active elapsed seconds, and the root-to-node path of the clock that fired. This evidence appears on RunResult , in every affected summary_tree node, and in their JSON forms. Developer obligation: Choose the name for what “took too long” means at that step. fail_after says the hardware did not do its job in time; abort_after says the harness gave up and no verdict exists. Never swallow asyncio.CancelledError ; doing so would obstruct every deadline declared above the await. Consequence: Fail at a deadline sends the Floor Technician to the hardware. Aborted at a deadline sends them to the harness. The composition names that distinction, and the record identifies the exact clock and budget without requiring the suite source.
docs.title: Time Budget Contract

docs.text: Framework obligation: Every failure must be traceable to one of the following root causes, made obvious by signal: 1. DUT failed a check — TestFailure from a test method or from configure() . State = Fail. A TestFailure from configure() carries an extra ambiguity: the device did not reach a testable state, but whether the cause is hardware or infrastructure cannot be determined from code. The framework surfaces the looking_for / failure message; the human triager decides. 2. Hardware lying — survey artifacts expose mismatch between claimed and actual state. 3. Test method bug — a plain exception from a test method or from configure() → all failure modes modeled by the developer must raise TestFailure . Anything else raised is a bug. Full stop. A missing verdict (non-PASS return) is likewise a contract violation, rendered as node-local Aborted because no verdict exists to report. 4. External integration failure — ExternalIntegrationFailure from a before_each / after_each hook. State = Aborted. 5. Operator interrupt — OperatorInterrupt from SIGINT/SIGTERM during a live run() . State = Aborted. The failure names the operator and the signal. Developer obligation: Use the right signal for the right category. - Raise TestFailure for any verdict — from a test method or from configure() — never a plain exception. - Use survey hooks to capture device-reported state at phase boundaries. - Use configure() for environment/readiness gating. A timeout there is a TestFailure whose cause (hardware vs. infrastructure) is for the human to determine — the framework will not pretend to know. - Let the framework raise ExternalIntegrationFailure — developers do not construct or raise it directly. It is raised automatically when a before_each / after_each hook throws anything.
docs.title: Failure Taxonomy Contract

docs.text: Framework obligation: Every run produces scoped, structured evidence automatically. - Logging is scoped to the current leaf test. - Survey and audit hooks share the same automatic artifact contract: every non- None return is faithfully recorded as an Artifact, including empty dicts, lists, and strings. Python resolves an explicit return None , a delegated call that returns None , and a fall-through to the same runtime value, so None writes only an informational log entry and no automatic artifact. When None itself is meaningful evidence, the SE must make that intent explicit with await utils.capture_artifact(Artifact(..., data=None)) inside the hook. - Once a hook returns a non- None observation, its automatic artifact publication is shielded from shutdown within its own 30-second evidence budget. Repeated cancellation cannot orphan an accepted observation after the hardware was read. - Survey dispatch points are the six members of Phase , in order: pre-configure , post-configure , pre-test , post-test , pre-cleanup , and post-cleanup , limited to the phases the lifecycle reaches. The artifact name identifies the dispatch point and registered-hook index; audit names identify both the hook and interval dispatch. Both use artifact type survey , keeping one Inspector evidence contract. - use_survey(fn, phases=...) schedules a survey at a subset of those points; the default is all six, and an empty selection is a ValueError at registration. A boundary the survey is not scheduled at writes one debug line and no artifact, so the run directory holds one artifact per boundary the survey was meant to observe. - Order is not reach. The phases are totally ordered, but after a failed configure the engine skips post-configure , pre-test , and post-test and still fires pre-cleanup and post-cleanup , with utils.exec on the test host if use_shell never returned. A survey that reads the device therefore guards on utils.exec_route , not on the phase; the phase says when, the route says where. - Log artifacts are co-located with their node. - Evidence travels with the verdict (issue #118). A leaf's readings leave its test method as PASS(evidence) or TestFailure(..., evidence=...) . The child boundary validates the payload entry by entry before it is recorded: a value that is not JSON, a key that shadows a ctx entry or the framework-owned measurements slot, or a key @evidence declared that PASS did not carry is a ContractViolation naming the leaf and the key. Nothing is stripped silently. A failure is not held to the declaration; it records what it was handed. - A leaf's RunResult.run_data is the JSON-safe view of its ctx plus the evidence its verdict carried, flat. A non-leaf node's run_data is the ctx view alone. Every summary_tree node carries evidence (what the leaf's verdict carried, or null) and evidence_declared (the @evidence declaration, or null); a declared key absent from evidence is a reading that was not taken, shown by name. - All serializable values (primitives, plain dicts, lists) configure() returned appear in run_data , except under a key the suite's redact_ctx claims (issue #154): that key appears with the value <REDACTED> , whatever it holds. The claims read the real value from utils.ctx ; the record does not carry it. - Functions, class instances, and live handles (e.g. SSH connections) are stripped from the ctx view; they are the objects a run works through, not evidence. - Context annotations do not bypass this filter. A TypedDict is an ordinary dict at runtime, and each value still has to satisfy the same serialization rules. - Filtering is all-or-nothing for each top-level ctx entry. A nested instance, handle, function, cycle, non-string mapping key, or non-finite float strips that complete entry; the framework never emits partial evidence or silently coerces it. - run_data is a detached snapshot taken when the node settles. An aborted leaf contributes no evidence; readings in hand when a time budget fires are lost by design, and the scoped log and point-in-time artifacts remain for in-flight observation. - run_data["measurements"] is framework-owned: the readings utils.measure recorded on this node, in call order, written when the node settles. An authored ctx entry with that name cannot populate or replace the slot, and a run_data override cannot drop it. Aggregation, SPC, and Cpk are the consumer's, not the record's. - Measurement Contract (issue #86, docs/measurements.md ). A limit is evidence, never a verdict: utils.measure records in_limits and touches neither the node's state nor its failure. A None value is admitted as a reading not taken (issue #159): recorded with value: null , never inside its window, so a claim gated on the window fails through its own gate. The framework refuses, as a ContractViolation naming the node and the measurement: an empty name, a bool , NaN , or infinite value, a non-text unit, or a window that bounds nothing or runs backwards; the same name recorded twice in one node; a call from outside configure() or the test method ( cleanup , surveys, audits, hooks, or after the node settled); and hilt.measure where no node's slot is executing. The record is sealed on every terminal state, Aborted included, and published on the node's run_data and on every summary_tree node ( null when the node never ran). A measurement does not satisfy an @evidence declaration. - Every RunResult includes ancestor_names: list[str] (path from root) and bread_crumbs: str (joined for display), plus a summary_tree snapshot of the node's subtree state at completion. Downstream integrators can reconstruct the full Inspector tree from the root's RunResult alone. - TestFailure , ExternalIntegrationFailure , and OperatorInterrupt all implement to_json() . Serializing a RunResult produces clean JSON for downstream integrators without any custom serializer. - Provenance. Every executed node records one exec routing: <where> (<why>) line — where is local or via <chain> , why names the call that put it there ( declared via use_shell , inherited from parent , declared via use_shell(inherit=False) ). A node that never declared a route renders where alone. The line is emitted after configure returns, since use_shell lives there and the route is not final until it does. - Every transport the router opens records its provenance lines as it comes up. SSH renders ssh connect: <user>@<host>:<port> auth=<label> via=<chain> ; via=direct means the connection dials out from the test host itself. When host-key verification is skipped, SSH records a second line, ssh host-key verification skipped: <host>:<port> , so the Floor Technician can see that verification was off without opening the suite. - Via chains are rendered in full and test-host-first ( bastion -> edge -> dut ), never summarized to the last hop. - The credential path is named exactly — key-file(/path) , agent(/socket) , password , key , none — and the credential's value never appears. What is logged is what was dialed: the resolution order is declared once, in SshInterface._auth_choice , and both the connect options and the provenance line read it. A password, private-key bytes, and the contents of a key file never reach the scoped log, run_data , the env snapshot, RunResult.to_json() , or a failure repr. - A suite's own secret is held to the same standard (issue #154). redact_ctx on the suite class names the ctx keys that are not for the record, exactly or as regular expressions matched against the whole key; a subclass adds to its bases' entries and never replaces them. A string under a redacted key is masked as <REDACTED> wherever it appears, run-wide: every scoped-log record, including one the author writes by hand; a failure's str() , repr() , and to_json() , down its cause chain, once the child boundary has recorded it; evidence on a verdict; captured artifacts; run_data ; and therefore RunResult.to_json() and every file in the run directory. Only a string is a needle; a number or a handle under a redacted key is shown as <REDACTED> in the ctx view and nothing more. The env snapshot stays verbatim (issue #53): a secret that is also in the environment is kept off the record with env_deny . Masking begins when the value enters ctx, by any write path ( configure() 's return, []= , update , setdefault , |= ), so a value logged inside configure() before it enters ctx is the author's to keep quiet. Masking is plain substring replacement, so a very short secret (a two-character token, a numeric sid such as 200 ) also masks unrelated text that happens to contain it; that fails closed and is accepted. - Consequence: the Floor Technician reconstructs the run's topology and its auth decisions from the artifacts alone, without opening the suite source. Developer obligation: Instrument appropriately. - Use utils.logger (never print ) so evidence is captured in artifacts. - Use self.use_survey() for periodic state snapshots; use await utils.capture_artifact(artifact) for point-in-time captures. Artifact is a write-free value on the public surface: the utility method is the only framework API that persists it, and it always emits the chronological pointer after publication. - Return structured data from use_survey / use_audit hooks to capture it as an artifact. - Hand readings back with the verdict: PASS({...}) or TestFailure(..., evidence={...}) . Declare with @evidence(...) what a pass must carry, beside the method that keeps the promise.
docs.title: Evidence Contract

docs.text: Framework obligation: Every full run() creates one timestamped run directory beneath the configured artifact root before the root lifecycle begins. Point-in-time artifacts and every per-node timeline live beneath that directory, so a run's evidence is self-contained and cannot overwrite a neighboring run. Every executed node that owns a discrete log streams the same records into two files: timeline.log , the human line view, and timeline.jsonl , the versioned Inspector record. Both files are flushed after every entry; an interrupted process therefore preserves every complete entry already accepted by the logger. The JSON Lines record carries one complete object per physical line with format_version , UTC timestamp , root-to-leaf scope , level , and message . Artifact-pointer records also carry artifact_name , artifact_path , artifact_type , and artifact_timestamp . A logging node opens its files lazily on its first record and closes them when that node reaches its terminal boundary. A declared node that never executes opens nothing. Authored suites, sequences, and parallel nodes own a log by default. Leaves roll up to the nearest owning ancestor. Sequences, parallel nodes, and composed suites may opt into the same roll-up with discrete_log_file=False ; a root still owns the run log. TestComponent.log_path exposes the owning node's absolute timeline.jsonl path after execution. It remains None for pending nodes and nodes whose records roll up. Every summary_tree node carries the same link as log_path , rendered as a POSIX path relative to the run directory, so the structural record reaches the temporal record without the live objects. It is null for pending nodes and nodes whose records roll up; the nearest ancestor with a link holds their chronology. On Pass, Fail, and Aborted, root run() atomically publishes the root RunResult.to_json() as result.json at the run-directory root before returning. The root timeline's final entry points to that file; a failed publication cannot expose a partial replacement or a pointer to evidence that was not published. The persisted chronology and root result are framework-owned. Developer code continues to use only utils.logger and utils.capture_artifact() ; it never opens or edits timeline or result files. Developer obligation: Do not write directly into the run directory or depend on its timestamped directory name. Treat log_path and captured artifact paths as opaque evidence references. The private _run_lifecycle() entry point is not a full run and therefore does not create a timestamped run directory. Framework self-tests that invoke it directly may leave point-in-time artifacts at the configured base root; authored suites use run() .
docs.title: Temporal Backbone Contract

docs.text: Framework obligation: When self.use_audit(interval=..., fn=...) is called in the constructor, the framework runs fn concurrently with the test methods on the specified interval. - Multiple audit hooks are supported — each runs on its own interval. - Every audit interval is validated during construction as positive and finite. An invalid registration cannot survive long enough to touch hardware. - Audit start/stop is framework-controlled, not caller-controlled: the loop begins immediately before the first test method runs and ends immediately after the last test method returns. No delayed start, no manual trigger. The lifecycle contract (test in runnable state before configure() returns) guarantees the audit's preconditions are met by start. - If the audit fn raises a TestFailure , the running test method is immediately cancelled and the test fails with the audit's failure. - Audit errors are not swallowed — unlike survey hooks, a throwing audit is a real failure. Survey and cleanup errors are swallowed to protect the hardware verdict; ExternalIntegrationFailure is exempt from swallowing everywhere — swallowing it would kill the halt signal. - Audit follows the same artifact contract as survey (see Evidence Contract above). - Cancellation is cooperative and asyncio-native.
