Both interfaces are framework-managed — no cleanup() override is needed. jump = await utils.get_shell(host=jump_host, username=jump_user) target = await utils.get_shell(host=target_host, username=target_user, via=jump) See examples/ssh_tunneling.py .
docs.title: SSH Tunneling

docs.text: A device API is not exec with a URL. Open a session from configure() with utils.get_http or utils.get_coap , then request a typed DeviceRequest . The response's status is data — HTTP 4xx/5xx is not an exception, and neither is a CoAP 4.xx. On HTTP, status is the integer. On CoAP it is the dotted code ( CoapCode.CONTENT is "2.05" ), which is what the record stores when the claim puts response.status on the verdict. Catch DeviceApiOperationFailure when the transfer itself did not complete (timeout, refused connection) and model it as a TestFailure . Retries default to zero. Each declared attempt is logged. POST refuses retry unless retry_non_idempotent=True . Attempt logs keep header names and withhold every value unless the author lists that name in evidence_headers . Abort closes the session; it does not invent a shutdown PUT. One handle carries one request at a time. Leaves under a parallel that share the handle configure() opened queue on it in call order — nothing collides and nothing is refused — so a round trip timed in the leaf includes the queue. A request still waiting when the handle is cancelled or closed is never sent; it fails with DeviceApiOperationFailure , the same class as any other transfer that did not complete. Measure the DUT alone with one handle per leaf. api = await utils.get_http(base_url="https://dut.local") response = await api.request(DeviceRequest(method="GET", path="/whoami")) if response.status != 200: raise TestFailure("whoami rejected", 200, response.status) return PASS({"status": response.status}) The backends stay off the public surface, the way SshInterface does. For a JSON body, declare json= instead of encoding bytes and setting a header by hand. Read it back with .json() , or select the parser with .parse(response_type="json") / .parse(response_type="yaml") (YAML needs hilt-core[yaml] ). Both leave the original bytes and status available. Parser errors propagate, so model a malformed response as TestFailure when it is a DUT failure mode. Neither the transfer nor the parser chooses a verdict. response = await api.request(DeviceRequest(method="PUT", path="/settings", json={"enabled": True})) if response.status == 200 and response.json().get("enabled") is True: return PASS({"enabled": True}) raise TestFailure("device did not enable", "enabled", response.status)
docs.title: Device API — CoAP/HTTP

docs.text: Where wait_for() is called determines what the timeout means , not what gets raised — both raise TestFailure : In configure() — timeout becomes a TestFailure that halts the lifecycle. The test lands in Fail; the suite never runs. The verdict means "the device did not reach a testable state." Whether the cause is hardware or infrastructure is not knowable from code — the human triager makes that call from logs and survey artifacts. In a test method — timeout becomes a TestFailure that is the verdict itself. The device was reachable but failed to reach the expected state. looking_for is required and must be plain language — it becomes the Floor Technician's primary diagnostic string when a wait times out. The call returns the predicate's truthy value ( True stays True ); a claim that needs what was observed returns it from the predicate instead of closing over a list. The runnable examples/wait_for_patterns.py ports both placements from the legacy example. It also shows how polling observations flow through scoped logs, phase-boundary surveys, point-in-time artifacts, run_data , and the root summary_tree without adding another evidence API.
docs.title: wait_for Patterns

docs.text: Inspector JSON Contract ¶ Floor Technicians reading a run should start at docs/floor-technician.md . This page is the consumer contract those fields live in. The Inspector TUI is outside the Python port's current scope. Its input contract is not. Every completed node produces a RunResult , and RunResult.to_json() returns a plain Python object that json.dumps() accepts without an encoder. The root result is self-contained: consumers do not need the live TestComponent objects to reconstruct the run tree. CI that already speaks JUnit XML consumes a projection of the same tree ( docs/junit-xml.md ); that reporter is not a second evidence record. Every full TestComponent.run() atomically writes the root RunResult.to_json() payload to result.json in the timestamped run directory beneath HILT_ARTIFACT_ROOT . The file is present for Pass, Fail, and Aborted outcomes. Its absolute path is published by the final entry in the root node's timeline, with artifact name result and artifact type run-result ; consumers do not need to derive the run directory name. Version 1 result ¶ Field JSON type Meaning format_version integer Schema version; currently 1 . state string One terminal state: Pass , Fail , or Aborted . failure object or null JSON-safe framework failure, including nested causes. timeout object or null Structured time-budget evidence when a deadline determined or contributed to this state. test_case string Stable name of this node. type string suite , test , parallel , or sequence : the node shape, in the vocabulary of build_suite . ancestor_names array of strings Root-to-this path, inclusive. bread_crumbs string Display path, exactly ancestor_names.join("/") . summary_tree object Recursive snapshot rooted at this node. physical_location string PHYSICAL_LOCATION , or unknown when absent. env object Environment snapshot taken at the start of the run, filtered per the run's allow or deny list; see below. run_data object Detached structured evidence snapshot: the JSON-safe view of the node's ctx, plus, on a leaf, the evidence its verdict carried. It always contains a framework-owned measurements array: one entry per utils.measure call on this node, in call order, empty when the node measured nothing. suite_target string or null The loader target that produced the run, as hilt run resolved it: an absolute suite file or module name, :: , and the suite class name. hilt inspect loads this suite for its Re-Run tab, so the technician re-runs a node with the code that ran in production; --suite overrides it. null when the run was started without one, from a developer's own harness. Added within version 1 on 2026-09-10; a consumer written before it treats the field as additive. A measurement entry is {name, value, unit, limits, in_limits, timestamp} as docs/measurements.md defines it: value is a number, or null when the suite tried to take the reading and could not (issue #159; a hole in the series, never a zero), limits is {low, high} with null for an open side or null altogether, in_limits is true , false (always false for a null value against a window), or null when no window was given, and timestamp is UTC ending in Z . in_limits is evidence, never a verdict; version 1 defines no aggregation, SPC, or Cpk, and an integrator must not infer them from the entries. Because result.json is the root's record, the entries a leaf recorded reach the file through measurements on its summary_tree node, not through this run_data . Python-only lifecycle details such as the internal slot and raw return value are not part of this payload. Consumers must treat unknown fields as additive and select a decoder by format_version (see Versioning policy ). The env snapshot is filtered by the run, not by the schema ¶ Version 1 publishes the run environment as the run declared it. TestComponent.run() and TestUtils accept either env_allow or env_deny (both is a ValueError ): a list of regular expressions matched with re.search against each variable's name . TOKEN therefore matches GITLAB_TOKEN ; anchor as ^HOME$ for an exact name. With an allow list only matching names are published; with a deny list matching names are withheld. Values are never hashed or rewritten — a variable is either present verbatim or absent. With neither list the snapshot is verbatim: every value present at run start, including tokens or credentials injected by CI or the shell, is serialized into the artifact. Keeping secrets out of an unfiltered run environment is the operator's obligation. DEBUG override. When the source environment carries environment=DEBUG , the declared list is ignored and every variable is published. The run logs a warning — DEBUG mode detected, ignoring provided <allow|deny> list and including ALL environment variables — so the artifact's extra content is explained in its own timeline. The filter is applied once, at the root, and every node and every RunResult sees the same filtered view. PHYSICAL_LOCATION and HILT_ARTIFACT_ROOT are read from that view, so an allow list must let them through to keep their effect. Decoders must not assume any particular variable is present (ruling on issue #53, 2026-09-03). Version 1 timeline ¶ Each run() creates a timestamped directory directly beneath HILT_ARTIFACT_ROOT . Point-in-time artifacts are stored at that run-directory root. Every executed node that owns a discrete log receives a child directory containing: timeline.log — a streamed human view with one escaped line per entry; timeline.jsonl — the authoritative Inspector record, with one complete JSON object per physical line. Both files are flushed after each entry. Consumers may read the JSON Lines file while a run is active and retain every complete line after interruption. The child-directory name is framework-owned and must be treated as opaque; use TestComponent.log_path rather than reconstructing it. Every version-1 timeline object contains these fields: Field JSON type Meaning format_version integer Timeline-record schema version; currently 1 . timestamp string Timezone-aware UTC timestamp ending in Z . scope array of strings Root-to-emitting-node path, inclusive. level string Lowercase Python logging level name. message string Fully rendered log message. Newlines remain escaped within the JSON line. An artifact-pointer entry additionally contains all four fields below. They are absent from ordinary records rather than set to null. Field JSON type Meaning artifact_name string Captured artifact name, or result for the root result. artifact_path string Absolute path of the published artifact or root result.json . artifact_type string Captured artifact type, or run-result for the root result. artifact_timestamp string The evidence timestamp in UTC; for the root result, its publication time. Authored suites, sequences, and parallel nodes own a log by default. Leaves roll their records into the nearest owning ancestor. A sequence, parallel node, or composed suite constructed with discrete_log_file=False also rolls up. Pending nodes create no files. Two records, two version fields ¶ A run therefore produces two versioned records, and each carries its own format_version : Record Where it lives Version field Result result.json at the run-directory root; the serialized root RunResult.to_json() and structural view rooted at summary_tree format_version on the result object Timeline timeline.jsonl beneath the run directory; the temporal view format_version on every JSON Lines object The two version numbers move independently. The summary tree links the structural view to the temporal view through each node's log_path (ruling on issue #106, 2026-09-04: the link is additive within result version 1). An Inspector selects a node in the tree, resolves log_path against the run directory, and reads that node's chronology. Versioning policy ¶ format_version is an integer on every record the framework emits: the result, every timeline line, and the envelope Artifact.to_json() writes for point-in-time evidence. One rule governs all of them. Additive within a version. Adding a field to a framework-owned object keeps the number. So does adding a key that the record already declares open ( env , run_data , and the failure object). A consumer must accept fields it does not know and must not fail on them; it reads what it was written for and ignores the rest. Breaking bumps the version. Removing or renaming a field, changing a field's JSON type or nullability, changing the meaning of an existing value, adding a member to a closed set ( state , type , declared , the failure state ), moving or renaming result.json or timeline.jsonl , or changing the one-object-per-line rule bumps the number. A bump is a contract change and follows the workflow in STANDARDS.md section 7: it is raised as an issue and ruled on before its MR opens. Consumers declare what they accept. A decoder reads format_version before any other field, accepts the versions it was written for, and refuses every other version loudly, with an error that names the version found and the versions accepted. A best-effort read of an unknown version is a silent misreading and is not permitted. Within an accepted version the decoder validates against the published schema for that version. The records version independently. Bumping the result does not bump the timeline, and the reverse. The per-node log_path link is additive within result version 1 (ruling on issue #106, 2026-09-04). Every change amends the schema in the same MR. A field added within version 1 appears in the version-1 schema and in this document before the framework emits it. The self-tests close every framework-owned object against its schema, so an emitted field the schema does not name is a red gate, not a silent contract change. A bump publishes a new schema file and leaves the previous one in place: a run directory written under version 1 stays readable by a version-1 consumer for as long as the record exists. Before 1.0.0 the record may change in place under version 1, because no consumer exists to break; the type vocabulary was renamed this way to match the composition vocabulary (ruling on issue #111, 2026-09-06), and measurements[].value became nullable this way for a reading not taken (ruling on issue #159, 2026-10-20). From 1.0.0 rule 2 applies as written. Published schemas ¶ Record Schema Draft Result docs/schema/result-v1.schema.json JSON Schema 2020-12 Timeline docs/schema/timeline-v1.schema.json JSON Schema 2020-12 Artifact envelope docs/schema/artifact-v1.schema.json JSON Schema 2020-12 The published files are the consumer contract, and they are open: framework-owned objects do not forbid additional properties, so a consumer validating with the file shipped in one release accepts the additive fields of a later release within the same version. Three objects are open by design and stay open under the self-tests as well: the failure object (a TestFailure subclass may add fields), env (station-defined names), and run_data (suite evidence beyond the framework-owned measurements slot). The measurement object itself is open as well, so a field added to it within version 1 is accepted by a consumer validating with this file. tests/test_inspector_schema.py validates every emitted result.json and every emitted timeline line against these files on each gate run, first as published and then with every framework-owned object closed. It also validates emitted point-in-time captures against the artifact-envelope schema with the envelope closed. That schema describes the existing Artifact.to_json() shape: format_version , name , type , timestamp , and data . The observation may be any JSON value, including explicit null. Additive envelope fields remain acceptable to consumers; the payload is never closed. The internal Inspector capture reader consumes this envelope under the same version policy. The root run-result pointer instead uses the result schema; it is not an envelope. Summary tree node ¶ Every summary_tree node contains exactly these version-1 fields: Field JSON type Meaning name string Stable node name. type string The same node-type discriminator used by RunResult . state string or null Terminal state, or null when a declared sequence step did not run. failure object or null JSON-safe failure for this exact node. timeout object or null Structured time-budget evidence for this exact node. log_path string or null POSIX path of this node's timeline.jsonl , relative to the run directory. Null when the node never ran or when its records rolled up into an ancestor. children array Ordered child nodes. Groups retain declaration order after settlement. evidence object or null The readings this leaf's verdict carried: PASS({...}) or TestFailure(..., evidence={...}) , validated entry by entry and detached. Null on a node that is not a leaf, that never ran, or whose verdict carried none. evidence_declared array of string or null The keys the leaf's @evidence declaration promised on PASS , in declaration order. A declared key absent from evidence is a reading that was not taken; show it by name. Null when the node is not a leaf or declared nothing. measurements array or null Every utils.measure call this node recorded, in call order, as measurement objects ( docs/measurements.md ). An array on every node that ran, empty when it measured nothing; null when the node never ran, matching state . A measurement does not satisfy an @evidence declaration and in_limits: false is not a Fail. A null tree state means pending/unreached; it is not a fourth terminal state. A stopped sequence retains its unexecuted descendants with null states, so the root snapshot still describes the full declared tree. log_path is relative so that a run directory copied to another machine keeps every link intact. Consumers resolve it against the run directory they opened, the same directory that holds the point-in-time artifacts. A node with a terminal state and a null log_path rolled its records into an ancestor; the nearest ancestor with a non-null log_path holds them, and the root always carries one. A node whose state is null never ran and has no chronology anywhere. Failure shape ¶ Failures use their framework to_json() methods. TestFailure and its subclasses retain the failure name, message, state, comparisons, and bug metadata. An ExternalIntegrationFailure retains its hook and JSON-safe cause. OperatorInterrupt retains operator: true and the signal name so a Ctrl-C is not mistaken for a hook failure. Arbitrary exception objects and live values degrade to descriptive JSON-safe forms rather than making serialization fail and masking the evidence. Timeout shape ¶ When no deadline contributed to a node's state, timeout is null. Otherwise it carries these fields: Field JSON type Meaning reason string Always timeout . declared string The winning declaration: fail_after or abort_after . budget_seconds number Positive finite duration declared on the winning clock. elapsed_seconds number Active window time consumed when that clock fired. clock string Root-to-declaring-node path of the winning clock. For fail_after , failure also contains the hardware-facing TestFailure . For abort_after , failure may be null because the framework does not forge a verdict; the timeout record carries the reason for the node-local Aborted state. Integrators should use ancestor_names as the durable node identity and bread_crumbs only for display. Names may contain / ; the array is therefore the canonical representation.
docs.title: Inspector JSON

docs.text: Floor Technicians reading a run should start at docs/floor-technician.md . This page is the consumer contract those fields live in. The Inspector TUI is outside the Python port's current scope. Its input contract is not. Every completed node produces a RunResult , and RunResult.to_json() returns a plain Python object that json.dumps() accepts without an encoder. The root result is self-contained: consumers do not need the live TestComponent objects to reconstruct the run tree. CI that already speaks JUnit XML consumes a projection of the same tree ( docs/junit-xml.md ); that reporter is not a second evidence record. Every full TestComponent.run() atomically writes the root RunResult.to_json() payload to result.json in the timestamped run directory beneath HILT_ARTIFACT_ROOT . The file is present for Pass, Fail, and Aborted outcomes. Its absolute path is published by the final entry in the root node's timeline, with artifact name result and artifact type run-result ; consumers do not need to derive the run directory name.
docs.title: Inspector JSON Contract

docs.text: Field JSON type Meaning format_version integer Schema version; currently 1 . state string One terminal state: Pass , Fail , or Aborted . failure object or null JSON-safe framework failure, including nested causes. timeout object or null Structured time-budget evidence when a deadline determined or contributed to this state. test_case string Stable name of this node. type string suite , test , parallel , or sequence : the node shape, in the vocabulary of build_suite . ancestor_names array of strings Root-to-this path, inclusive. bread_crumbs string Display path, exactly ancestor_names.join("/") . summary_tree object Recursive snapshot rooted at this node. physical_location string PHYSICAL_LOCATION , or unknown when absent. env object Environment snapshot taken at the start of the run, filtered per the run's allow or deny list; see below. run_data object Detached structured evidence snapshot: the JSON-safe view of the node's ctx, plus, on a leaf, the evidence its verdict carried. It always contains a framework-owned measurements array: one entry per utils.measure call on this node, in call order, empty when the node measured nothing. suite_target string or null The loader target that produced the run, as hilt run resolved it: an absolute suite file or module name, :: , and the suite class name. hilt inspect loads this suite for its Re-Run tab, so the technician re-runs a node with the code that ran in production; --suite overrides it. null when the run was started without one, from a developer's own harness. Added within version 1 on 2026-09-10; a consumer written before it treats the field as additive. A measurement entry is {name, value, unit, limits, in_limits, timestamp} as docs/measurements.md defines it: value is a number, or null when the suite tried to take the reading and could not (issue #159; a hole in the series, never a zero), limits is {low, high} with null for an open side or null altogether, in_limits is true , false (always false for a null value against a window), or null when no window was given, and timestamp is UTC ending in Z . in_limits is evidence, never a verdict; version 1 defines no aggregation, SPC, or Cpk, and an integrator must not infer them from the entries. Because result.json is the root's record, the entries a leaf recorded reach the file through measurements on its summary_tree node, not through this run_data . Python-only lifecycle details such as the internal slot and raw return value are not part of this payload. Consumers must treat unknown fields as additive and select a decoder by format_version (see Versioning policy ).
docs.title: Version 1 result

docs.text: Version 1 publishes the run environment as the run declared it. TestComponent.run() and TestUtils accept either env_allow or env_deny (both is a ValueError ): a list of regular expressions matched with re.search against each variable's name . TOKEN therefore matches GITLAB_TOKEN ; anchor as ^HOME$ for an exact name. With an allow list only matching names are published; with a deny list matching names are withheld. Values are never hashed or rewritten — a variable is either present verbatim or absent. With neither list the snapshot is verbatim: every value present at run start, including tokens or credentials injected by CI or the shell, is serialized into the artifact. Keeping secrets out of an unfiltered run environment is the operator's obligation. DEBUG override. When the source environment carries environment=DEBUG , the declared list is ignored and every variable is published. The run logs a warning — DEBUG mode detected, ignoring provided <allow|deny> list and including ALL environment variables — so the artifact's extra content is explained in its own timeline. The filter is applied once, at the root, and every node and every RunResult sees the same filtered view. PHYSICAL_LOCATION and HILT_ARTIFACT_ROOT are read from that view, so an allow list must let them through to keep their effect. Decoders must not assume any particular variable is present (ruling on issue #53, 2026-09-03).
docs.title: The env snapshot is filtered by the run, not by the schema

docs.text: Each run() creates a timestamped directory directly beneath HILT_ARTIFACT_ROOT . Point-in-time artifacts are stored at that run-directory root. Every executed node that owns a discrete log receives a child directory containing: timeline.log — a streamed human view with one escaped line per entry; timeline.jsonl — the authoritative Inspector record, with one complete JSON object per physical line. Both files are flushed after each entry. Consumers may read the JSON Lines file while a run is active and retain every complete line after interruption. The child-directory name is framework-owned and must be treated as opaque; use TestComponent.log_path rather than reconstructing it. Every version-1 timeline object contains these fields: Field JSON type Meaning format_version integer Timeline-record schema version; currently 1 . timestamp string Timezone-aware UTC timestamp ending in Z . scope array of strings Root-to-emitting-node path, inclusive. level string Lowercase Python logging level name. message string Fully rendered log message. Newlines remain escaped within the JSON line. An artifact-pointer entry additionally contains all four fields below. They are absent from ordinary records rather than set to null. Field JSON type Meaning artifact_name string Captured artifact name, or result for the root result. artifact_path string Absolute path of the published artifact or root result.json . artifact_type string Captured artifact type, or run-result for the root result. artifact_timestamp string The evidence timestamp in UTC; for the root result, its publication time. Authored suites, sequences, and parallel nodes own a log by default. Leaves roll their records into the nearest owning ancestor. A sequence, parallel node, or composed suite constructed with discrete_log_file=False also rolls up. Pending nodes create no files.
docs.title: Version 1 timeline

docs.text: A run therefore produces two versioned records, and each carries its own format_version : Record Where it lives Version field Result result.json at the run-directory root; the serialized root RunResult.to_json() and structural view rooted at summary_tree format_version on the result object Timeline timeline.jsonl beneath the run directory; the temporal view format_version on every JSON Lines object The two version numbers move independently. The summary tree links the structural view to the temporal view through each node's log_path (ruling on issue #106, 2026-09-04: the link is additive within result version 1). An Inspector selects a node in the tree, resolves log_path against the run directory, and reads that node's chronology.
docs.title: Two records, two version fields

docs.text: format_version is an integer on every record the framework emits: the result, every timeline line, and the envelope Artifact.to_json() writes for point-in-time evidence. One rule governs all of them. Additive within a version. Adding a field to a framework-owned object keeps the number. So does adding a key that the record already declares open ( env , run_data , and the failure object). A consumer must accept fields it does not know and must not fail on them; it reads what it was written for and ignores the rest. Breaking bumps the version. Removing or renaming a field, changing a field's JSON type or nullability, changing the meaning of an existing value, adding a member to a closed set ( state , type , declared , the failure state ), moving or renaming result.json or timeline.jsonl , or changing the one-object-per-line rule bumps the number. A bump is a contract change and follows the workflow in STANDARDS.md section 7: it is raised as an issue and ruled on before its MR opens. Consumers declare what they accept. A decoder reads format_version before any other field, accepts the versions it was written for, and refuses every other version loudly, with an error that names the version found and the versions accepted. A best-effort read of an unknown version is a silent misreading and is not permitted. Within an accepted version the decoder validates against the published schema for that version. The records version independently. Bumping the result does not bump the timeline, and the reverse. The per-node log_path link is additive within result version 1 (ruling on issue #106, 2026-09-04). Every change amends the schema in the same MR. A field added within version 1 appears in the version-1 schema and in this document before the framework emits it. The self-tests close every framework-owned object against its schema, so an emitted field the schema does not name is a red gate, not a silent contract change. A bump publishes a new schema file and leaves the previous one in place: a run directory written under version 1 stays readable by a version-1 consumer for as long as the record exists. Before 1.0.0 the record may change in place under version 1, because no consumer exists to break; the type vocabulary was renamed this way to match the composition vocabulary (ruling on issue #111, 2026-09-06), and measurements[].value became nullable this way for a reading not taken (ruling on issue #159, 2026-10-20). From 1.0.0 rule 2 applies as written.
docs.title: Versioning policy

docs.text: Record Schema Draft Result docs/schema/result-v1.schema.json JSON Schema 2020-12 Timeline docs/schema/timeline-v1.schema.json JSON Schema 2020-12 Artifact envelope docs/schema/artifact-v1.schema.json JSON Schema 2020-12 The published files are the consumer contract, and they are open: framework-owned objects do not forbid additional properties, so a consumer validating with the file shipped in one release accepts the additive fields of a later release within the same version. Three objects are open by design and stay open under the self-tests as well: the failure object (a TestFailure subclass may add fields), env (station-defined names), and run_data (suite evidence beyond the framework-owned measurements slot). The measurement object itself is open as well, so a field added to it within version 1 is accepted by a consumer validating with this file. tests/test_inspector_schema.py validates every emitted result.json and every emitted timeline line against these files on each gate run, first as published and then with every framework-owned object closed. It also validates emitted point-in-time captures against the artifact-envelope schema with the envelope closed. That schema describes the existing Artifact.to_json() shape: format_version , name , type , timestamp , and data . The observation may be any JSON value, including explicit null. Additive envelope fields remain acceptable to consumers; the payload is never closed. The internal Inspector capture reader consumes this envelope under the same version policy. The root run-result pointer instead uses the result schema; it is not an envelope.

docs.text: HILT Inspector — target specification ¶ This is the first deliverable of #89 . It carries the legacy Floor Technician guide into the Python port, adjusted for the signed decisions on #88 , #106 , and #107 . It specifies the terminal UI, which hilt inspect now opens. The Floor Technician guide remains the station page for reading the evidence by hand. The review rulings on !119 set the implementation order: Inspect first, Run as a separate increment behind its own decision. Ty ruled on that increment on 2026-09-10: the Re-Run tab ships, the Failures list is folded into Inspect as a key that hides passing rows, and the cut between the two tabs is the one the legacy tool drew. Inspect is the archive of the production run and executes nothing. Re-Run is the bench, where a node is executed again with the code that ran in production and nothing it produces persists. The internal timeline reader ( hilt.inspector_timeline.TimelineReader ) is implemented as a foundation for the log pane. It asynchronously reads a selected timeline path, validates each version-1 object against the packaged published schema, and returns records and line-numbered diagnostics in physical order. Additive fields and recorded scopes and pointers survive unchanged. A complete final JSON object is readable without a trailing newline; an unfinished final object or UTF-8 sequence produces a truncation diagnostic. Malformed complete records, duplicate keys, non-finite numbers, and unsupported versions are explicit diagnostics, and later valid records remain readable. Missing or unreadable logs produce a file-level unavailable diagnostic. These are reader observations, never test verdicts. The timeline reader does not open artifact pointers or resolve tree ownership. Its read_reference(run_root, reference) boundary opens a recorded POSIX log_path only beneath the selected run directory, preserving the complete relative path after a move. Empty, absolute, traversing, missing, non-file, and symlink-escaping references produce unavailable diagnostics. The read retains the recorded reference and the resolved source path; a reference that cannot resolve has no source path. It never searches another directory for a matching basename. Timeline and capture readers share one checked, cached loader for the packaged schemas; evidence is read afresh on every call. The operator's selected run directory may itself use symlinks or .. ; the reader resolves that directory before containing recorded links. The internal capture reader ( hilt.inspector_artifacts.ArtifactReader ) now reads absolute pointers beneath an opened run root. An explicit, established original root enables relocation while preserving the full relative tail; without that mapping a pointer outside the opened root is unavailable. The reader checks resolved containment, refuses non-file targets, and never falls back to the original run or a basename match. It validates the artifact envelope or root result against its packaged version-1 schema, retaining additive fields and explicit null observations. Missing files, malformed JSON, and unsupported versions are diagnostics that retain the recorded reference. JSON parsing is shared with the timeline reader, so duplicate keys and non-finite values are refused consistently. The original-root mapping remains an input to this internal component; the saved-run loader establishes it from publication evidence. The internal tree reader ( hilt.inspector_tree.TreeReader ) now opens a selected result through that validated result boundary. It resolves the operator's selection before deriving the run root, so a symlink such as latest/result.json or a path with .. opens the same saved evidence as its direct path. References inside saved records still obey the capture reader's traversal and containment checks. read_selected() retains the resolved run directory alongside the validated tree; read() returns just that tree through the same selection boundary. Unresolvable operator paths produce unavailable diagnostics in either form. Its InspectorTree preserves every recorded node in declaration preorder, including pending descendants, and keeps full name components rather than splitting display breadcrumbs. Stable row indices keep duplicate names distinct. Inspect selection and the Failures projection share the same rows: previous/next failure includes Fail and Aborted, skips Pass and pending, and does not wrap. The model retains failure causes, timeout fields, and additive evidence; declared readings absent from evidence are exposed by name, while null and zero remain present observations. For an executed selection, the model identifies its own or nearest ancestor's recorded timeline link. A pending selection has no owner and must render not run . An owner identifies a recorded link, not proof the file is available: the model opens no timeline, and its caller must still enforce run-root containment and report unavailable files. The internal selection model ( hilt.inspector_selection.InspectorSelection ) joins that tree to contained timeline loading for both Inspect and Failures. Its caller supplies the validated tree and the opened directory containing that same result, then navigates through the selection model. Selection clears the previous chronology before I/O, keeps the claim and its recorded owner together, and reads only through read_reference . Every request has its own identity: a delayed load cannot overwrite a later selection, even if the cursor returned to the same row. Pending rows render not run ; executed rows with no owner or an unreadable file render log unavailable . Complete records, their scopes, partial reads, and decoding diagnostics remain intact. Reselection reads evidence afresh. Cancellation and reader defects propagate to the caller and return only the affected current load to idle; they never restore an earlier log or become verdicts. The internal saved-run loader ( hilt.inspector_run.SavedRunReader ) now opens a validated result, its contained root timeline, and a capture reader for that same run. It uses TreeReader.read_selected() so selection errors and the resolved run boundary have one owner. The tree's chronology ownership also governs this opening: a pending root supplies no timeline or relocation origin, even if a damaged record gives it a link. It establishes the original root only from one final root-scoped pointer with artifact_type="run-result" , artifact_name="result" , and an absolute, non-traversing path to result.json . The result's ancestor names must agree with its tree root; full name components are compared without splitting breadcrumbs, and a disagreement names the result defect instead of directing the technician to the log. A missing, damaged, ambiguous, or misplaced publication leaves the original root explicitly unavailable while preserving the saved tree and timeline diagnostics. Complete records without a trailing newline remain readable. The loader never guesses from a basename or timestamp, reads the original station, or edits saved pointers. Reopening reads the evidence afresh. Without a mapping, captures already beneath the opened root remain readable, but pointers outside it cannot relocate. The internal timeline presentation model ( hilt.inspector_timeline_view.TimelineView ) pages a completed selection's chronology without changing its recorded data. It opens at the tail with filtering off; toggling errors returns to the first page. The filter retains Python error and critical records (case-insensitively) and every reader diagnostic. Custom levels have no inferred severity and remain in the full view. Each page retains physical line numbers, scopes, timestamps, and additive fields. Resizing changes the number of records per page and clamps the current page; an empty projection has one empty page. The terminal supplies that size after reserving its header and controls. This model counts records, not wrapped terminal lines. Structured pointers receive one-based numbers across the complete loaded chronology, before paging or filtering. Lookup keeps the same target even when its row is hidden; message text never supplies a path. An empty recorded path remains numbered so the capture reader can diagnose it. All numbers remain addressable, including those above the 1 – 9 direct shortcuts. The returned record supplies the pointer fields to the saved run's capture reader, including the distinct run-result decoding kind. A new completed selection read gets a fresh presentation model; selection/load state remains owned by InspectorSelection . The moved 70-DUT test exercises this composition without executing suite code or changing saved bytes. The internal artifact navigation model ( hilt.inspector_artifact_navigation.ArtifactNavigation ) now groups the complete timeline's numbered pointers by recorded type. Types follow first appearance; captures within a type retain chronology order. Opening selects exactly the requested number, including one above nine or hidden by a filter; an invalid number is rejected instead of opening another capture. Single-view type navigation wraps and selects the new type's first capture, while capture navigation clamps at either end. Diff selection requires at least two captures of the same type. It starts with the single-view capture on the left and the first other capture on the right. The bracket actions cycle the left target and the arrow actions cycle the right target within that type. When a move reaches the other target, the two sides swap; they never collapse onto one capture. Leaving diff restores the original single-view selection. Targets retain their timeline number, full pointer record, recorded reference, and decoding kind for the existing contained capture reader. Empty paths remain selectable and produce that reader's unavailable diagnostic. A moved 70-DUT test opens null and named captures and the root result without suite execution or saved-byte changes. The internal artifact modal model ( hilt.inspector_artifact_view.ArtifactModal ) joins that selection to the saved run's capture reader and pages what it reads. A capture is printed in its recorded key order, so two captures of one type line up; an unavailable or undecodable capture shows the reader's diagnostic with the recorded reference and is never replaced by another file. In diff mode the two captures are aligned row by row and one page cursor moves both sides together, as the artifact table above specifies; a singleton type stays single without a reload, and every change of selection returns to the first page because a capture is read from its top. A delayed read never replaces a newer selection, in the pattern of the selection model. The shared 70-DUT recording in tests/inspector_rack.py proves the composition without suite execution or saved-byte changes. The main view ( hilt.inspector_app.InspectorApp ) is the first terminal screen, built on Textual by Ty's ruling of 2026-09-09. It renders the tab row, the tree, and the chronology pane from the models above and forwards the quick-reference keys, one model call per key: Inspect and Re-Run share one cursor, the chronology loads on cursor movement without Enter and names its owner when the node's records rolled up, the owner's row carries the cyan arrow, arrows jump between Fail and Aborted rows without wrapping, h hides passing rows, n / p page, and f filters to errors while a truncation marker stays in place. Tree depth is drawn with the legacy glyphs ( ├─ , └─ , │ ), computed over the rows on screen so a hidden branch still closes on its last visible child. The plain text of every redraw is kept on the app so the self-tests drive it against the recorded runs in tests/inspector_rack.py and a screenshot can be read back against this guide. The re-run session ( hilt.inspector_rerun.RerunSession ) is the adapter behind the Re-Run tab. It receives a suite factory from the command line, never a suite derived from evidence; loads it on the tab's first opening, off the event loop; refuses a suite whose declared tree differs from the saved one, naming the first row that differs; executes the pressed node through TestComponent.run(subtree=...) , the sealed lifecycle with every leaf outside that subtree left pending; reads the result back through the same saved-run reader the archive uses, so the tab shows a re-run's states and chronology with the same code paths; and keeps that evidence under a scratch directory emptied per node on each re-run and removed when the Inspector closes. Interrupting a live re-run raises the operator signal, so the framework's own termination contract settles the node Aborted with bounded cleanup. The artifact modal screen ( hilt.inspector_app.ArtifactScreen ) opens from a digit in the log pane over the capture carrying that number and owns the artifact keys until b closes it: [ and ] move between types or the left side of a comparison, the arrows between captures of the type or the right side, n and p page both sides together, d enters and leaves the comparison. It renders the modal model only: one capture as its lines, a comparison as two aligned columns with differing rows highlighted, a diagnostic as the reader's words with the recorded reference. The entry point is hilt inspect [PATH] ( hilt.cli ): PATH is a run directory or its result.json ; without PATH the most recently modified result.json under the artifact root opens ( HILT_ARTIFACT_ROOT , default artifacts/ ; --artifact-root DIR overrides), the legacy discovery rule carried over. Nothing under the root, or a selection that is not a saved version-1 run, is refused with the reader's diagnostic on stderr and exit status 3. Opening runs no suite code. --suite TARGET names the suite the Re-Run tab executes, in the form hilt run accepts, and is loaded at the prompt so a wrong target is exit 3 there; without it the tab uses the suite_target the run recorded, loaded only when the tab is first opened. The Inspector serves the person at the station when a test stops the line. Its test of success is concrete: find what happened, categorize it, and begin the station's recovery protocol within sixty seconds, without opening suite source. What the Inspector reads ¶ Inspect mode replays saved evidence. Moving the cursor, paging a log, opening an artifact, or comparing two captures never touches the DUT and never executes suite code. The input is a run directory containing result.json , its per-node timeline.jsonl files, and the point-in-time artifacts referenced by those timelines. The structural tree comes entirely from summary_tree ; the temporal view comes entirely from the linked JSON Lines records. A saved 70-DUT rack must be inspectable without live TestComponent objects, source discovery, an SSH connection, or the test station that produced it. The Inspector JSON contract owns the field definitions and version policy. This page owns their presentation. It introduces no new result fields or verdict rules. The result and each timeline record have independent format_version values; select and validate each decoder separately, accept additive fields, and report unsupported versions explicitly rather than guessing their meaning. Opening a run ¶ hilt inspect PATH opens a selected result.json , or the result.json inside a selected run directory, and treats its containing directory as the run root. hilt inspect alone opens the most recently modified result.json under the artifact root ( HILT_ARTIFACT_ROOT , default artifacts/ ; --artifact-root DIR overrides), the legacy convenience carried over by Ty's ruling of 2026-09-09 on #89. The legacy npm run inspect command and summary-tree.artifact input are not Python interfaces. If no result is available, explain that there is no saved tree to inspect. Do not start a test to manufacture one: hilt inspect with nothing under the root exits 3 saying so, and a selection that is not a saved version-1 run exits 3 with the reader's diagnostic, never another file opened in its place. Absence of result.json is not a verdict: an invocation may have failed before a run, or a process may have ended before result publication. Preserve any surviving timeline evidence for diagnosis. The screen layout ¶ The terminal has a tab bar, the tree above, and the highlighted node's timeline below. This illustration shows the arrangement, not a captured run: [ Inspect ] Re-Run --------------------------------------------------------- rack Aborted └─ servers Aborted ← ├─ server-01 Pass ├─ server-02 Fail > │ └─ thermal check Fail not taken: fan_rpm ├─ server-03 Aborted └─ firmware check Pending --------------------------------------------------------- log: rack/servers (rolled up: thermal check has no own log) page 4/7 errors only: off captures: 1 (1-9 opens a capture) 14:02:11Z info starting thermal ramp [1] 14:02:45Z info survey captured 14:03:02Z error temperature 87 C exceeds 75 C q Quit Tab Inspect / Re-Run ← → failures h Hide passes n p page f Errors only The log updates on cursor movement. Enter is never required to read it. A delayed load for the previous selection must not overwrite the currently highlighted node's view. Show the selected node and, when different, the ancestor that owns its timeline: the pane names that owner, and the owner's row ends in the cyan ← so the eye finds the file the highlighted node's records went into. Depth is drawn with the legacy glyphs: ├─ for a child with siblings below it, └─ for the last child, │ continuing a branch that has more children further down. They are computed over the rows on screen, so when passing rows are hidden each remaining branch still closes on its last visible child. Tree order is declaration order, including in parallel compositions. A parent marked Fail may summarize a failing child; keep the descendants visible so the technician can reach the actual claim. Use the root-to-node array of names as the path, not a split of the display breadcrumbs: names may themselves contain / . The tabs ¶ Inspect — the default ¶ Display every declared node, with its recorded state and failure message. Color and symbols help scanning, but the state must remain legible as text. State Presentation and meaning Pass Green success mark. The framework accepted an explicit verdict and any required evidence. A string "PASS" is not a passing verdict. Fail Red failure mark. Read the failure object: this can be a modeled TestFailure or a software contract violation. Aborted Distinct, named state. No verdict was produced; the cause may be integration, operator interrupt, missing verdict, or an abort budget. null Dim Pending / unreached row. This declared step never ran; it is not a fourth terminal state. Left and right arrows move backward and forward through nodes needing attention, skipping Pass and pending rows. Preserve the legacy implementation's inclusion of both Fail and Aborted in that navigation, while keeping their labels and recovery meanings distinct. At either end, leave the cursor where it is; do not wrap unexpectedly. h hides every Pass row and shows them again. This replaces the legacy Failures list (Ty, 2026-09-10): the same recorded tree with the passing branches folded away, so a failure buried inside a large rack is found without leaving the tree or losing its place in it. Pending rows stay visible; they are not passes. If the cursor was on a row that just disappeared, it lands on the nearest visible row above it. When every node passed, the pane says so rather than showing nothing. Show the selected leaf's evidence beside its claim and failure. For every name in evidence_declared absent from evidence , show not taken by name. An absent reading is neither zero nor a successful measurement. Do not present the reserved empty run_data["measurements"] slot as an implemented measurement or SPC feature. Re-Run — the bench ¶ The same tree, unhydrated: every row reads not re-run until the technician executes it. Move to any node and press Enter to execute that node and everything beneath it with the code that ran in production. Switching tabs or highlighting a node never runs anything; Enter on the Inspect tab does nothing. The purpose is the floor's quick check: the ping failed, the cable is reseated, the one claim is re-run with the production code, and only then is the whole suite restarted through the station's normal procedure. What executes is the sealed lifecycle, confined to one subtree. TestComponent.run takes subtree= , the child positions from the root to the pressed node. Every node on the path to it runs its own configure and cleanup, because that is their lifecycle and the only way the pressed node meets the hop its ancestors own; every leaf outside the subtree is left pending, never executed. The framework continues to own configure and cleanup. This is not the legacy ↑ctx ancestor-configure replay, which stays prohibited: no parent's configure is replayed outside the lifecycle to make a device runnable, and the instance-local context idiom is untouched. The suite is supplied, never derived. hilt run records the loader target it used in result.json as suite_target (absolute file or module name, :: , class), and hilt inspect loads that suite the first time the tab is opened; --suite TARGET names another, and is loaded at the prompt. Nothing is reconstructed from result.json , artifact contents, or source found beside the run directory. Before any node runs, the supplied suite's declared tree is compared with the saved one, name and type in preorder; a difference is refused by path, and the pane says which suite to name instead. A run that recorded no target, one started from a developer's own harness, leaves the tab unavailable with that reason until --suite is given. Nothing the bench produces persists. Each re-run writes its evidence under a scratch directory, in a subdirectory per pressed node. Re-running the same node empties that subdirectory first, so the ninth re-run leaves nothing of the eighth. The whole scratch directory is removed when the Inspector closes. After a re-run the pressed node and its descendants that ran show their fresh states; rows the re-run never reached keep whatever an earlier re-run left, or not re-run . The log pane shows the highlighted node's re-run chronology, read by the same reader as the archive, with the same owner arrow; a node no re-run reached says so instead of borrowing the archive's log. A node above the pressed one reads partly re-run, never a verdict. Its lifecycle ran and its chronology is worth reading, but the state it rolled up covers only the child the bench was pointed at: every sibling was left pending and contributed nothing to it. Drawn as a verdict, that rollup turns a group whose other child failed in production into a Pass and carries the Pass to the root, which is the one reading the floor must never be given (issue #141). The bench answers for the branch it ran; the verdict on the whole node belongs to the archive on the Inspect tab, or to a re-run of that node, which runs every claim beneath it and so reads as a verdict again. The run's recorded environment seeds the re-run, so the station's variables travel with the record; the live environment overrides it, so a technician can change one deliberately before pressing Enter. A live re-run is live hardware. Tab is held while a node runs, as in the legacy UI, and Enter starts nothing else. q during a re-run is the operator interrupt: it takes the framework's termination contract , the node settles Aborted with bounded cleanup, and only then does the Inspector exit. A second q during that cleanup exits immediately, as a second signal does at the station. The legacy promise that Ctrl-C always exits immediately with nothing at stake applies to the archive, not to the bench. The main workflow: diagnosing a failure ¶ Find the node needing attention. Use right/left to move forward/backward without scrolling through passed leaves. Read the recorded state before choosing a recovery. Read the failure message and comparison. Show fail_message , and expected / received when present. Preserve bug banners, nested causes, hook names, and operator signals; a plain-language message alone does not establish hardware fault. Read the timeline already below the tree. n advances a page, p returns a page, and f toggles the errors-only filter. Log severity does not replace the verdict. Open a referenced artifact. Press its displayed digit, 1 – 9 . Survey captures can show whether the device's reported health agrees with what actually happened. Choose the recovery protocol. Read the failure's cause and the available evidence. The human makes the final determination; uncertainty is a reason to escalate. The five categories follow the current Failure Taxonomy Contract , which supersedes the legacy guide's separate, automatically assigned infrastructure category: Category Evidence to read Recovery direction DUT failed a check Modeled TestFailure , comparisons, and captured readings. A configure failure means the device did not reach a testable state; hardware versus infrastructure remains a human determination. Follow the station protocol for the established cause. Hardware lying Survey evidence contradicts a claimed healthy state or the apparent verdict. Preserve the discrepancy and seek deeper inspection, even after Pass. Test method bug Contract-violation banner, bug , or MissingVerdict . The latter is Aborted; thrown bugs are Fail. A framework-contract banner identifies the framework maintainer as the owner. Escalate the software defect; do not condemn the unit from this signal. External integration failure ExternalIntegrationFailure , its hook, and its cause. Restore the harness or coordination service before retrying. Operator interrupt OperatorInterrupt , operator: true , and its signal. The rack was stopped deliberately; resume only under the station's procedure. Time-budget evidence supplements this taxonomy. Display the winning timeout.clock , declaration, budget, and elapsed time. fail_after produces Fail; abort_after produces Aborted and may have no failure object at all. Do not relabel the latter as a hook failure just because both are Aborted. The station recovery table gives the full reading procedure. The timeline and its owner ¶ Resolve a node's non-null log_path relative to the selected run directory. A terminal node with a null link rolled its records into the nearest ancestor with a link; indicate that ancestor with the legacy cyan owner arrow. Keep each entry's scope visible so sibling records in the shared timeline cannot be mistaken for this leaf's readings. A pending node has no chronology anywhere. Show not run , not its parent's timeline as though the pending node produced evidence. A missing file for a node that did run is a separate, explicit log unavailable condition. Neither condition changes state. Read JSON Lines incrementally, preserving file order and every complete valid record. For an interrupted final line, display the complete preceding records and a visible truncation marker; do not fill in the unfinished object. Report malformed complete records or unsupported versions as decoding errors rather than silently dropping them. An errors-only filter must not hide these reader diagnostics. Artifacts — the evidence behind the verdict ¶ Number structured artifact-pointer entries in the loaded timeline and show [N] on the corresponding row. Digits 1 – 9 open the matching numbered capture in a modal. Take the link from the pointer fields, not from a path-looking substring in message . Retain numbering when paging or filtering so a digit never silently changes its target. The modal groups captures by artifact_type and labels each with its name and timestamp. Show the persisted content, including an explicit null observation; nothing in the viewer recomputes a verdict. The root run-result pointer opens result.json , whose shape differs from a point-in-time artifact envelope. The capture reader checks the envelope's own version and published schema as required by the JSON version policy . An unavailable or unreadable capture produces a visible diagnostic containing the reference, while the log and tree remain usable. The saved files are never edited. Version 1 stores absolute artifact_path pointers, whereas tree log links are relative. The reader resolves captures under the selected run root. For a moved run, try re-anchoring the recorded path's run-root-relative tail beneath the opened run root before declaring the capture unavailable. Preserve that full relative path: two nodes may capture different evidence with the same filename. Never search for or substitute a file merely because its basename matches. Re-anchoring requires an established original run root. If the reader cannot establish that mapping, or the mapped capture cannot be read under the opened root, show artifact unavailable with the recorded reference; do not guess a root or silently fall back to another run's evidence. The reader implementation must demonstrate that mapping and its unavailable cases in tests before claiming moved-run support. This is a reader rule. Saved pointers remain unchanged and absolute at version 1. Changing their stored representation to relative paths is a record-contract change under the version policy , requiring Ty's decision before an implementation MR. Reading and comparing artifacts ¶ Key Single-artifact view Diff view [ / ] Previous / next artifact type. Change the left artifact within the current type. ← / → Previous / next artifact within the current type. Change the right artifact within the current type. n / p Next / previous content page. Page both sides together. d Enter diff when the type has at least two artifacts. Return to the single-artifact view. b Close the modal and return to the log. Close the modal and return to the log. Diff shows two captures of the same type side by side, highlighting changed lines and dimming unchanged lines. Preserve the legacy guide's intended swap when the two selected indices collide, so a two-capture comparison can reverse sides. This is a display of recorded differences, not an automatic diagnosis of hardware truth. Key bindings quick reference ¶ Context Key Action Saved inspection, including a modal q / Ctrl-C Quit without changing evidence or touching hardware. Live re-run q / Ctrl-C Operator interrupt: the node settles Aborted through bounded cleanup, then the Inspector exits. A second press during cleanup exits at once. Main view Tab Switch Inspect / Re-Run. Held during a live re-run. Either tree ↑ / ↓ Move through the rows on screen; hidden passes are stepped over. Either tree ← / → Previous / next Fail or Aborted node of the saved run; skip passed and pending rows. Inspect tree h Hide passing rows, or show them again. Re-Run tree Enter Execute the highlighted node and everything beneath it; nothing else runs anything. Log pane, no modal n / p Next / previous page. Log pane, no modal f Toggle errors-only filtering. Log pane, no modal 1 – 9 Open the artifact carrying that number. Artifact modal b , [ , ] , ← , → , n , p , d Use the artifact controls above; the modal owns these keys until it closes. Things that need careful reading ¶ An ancestor owns the log. The owner arrow explains roll-up; it says nothing about context inheritance. The legacy ↑ctx ancestor-configure replay is prohibited. An error appears in a passing test. Survey errors are logged but do not decide the verdict. Read the state and the surrounding capture, not just the line's color. Many nodes are Aborted. An integration halt or operator interruption can affect the whole in-flight tree. A missing verdict or an abort budget is node-local. Read the cause instead of inferring a rack-wide hardware failure from repeated labels. The record ends abruptly. Retain the accepted chronology and mark the missing tail. Neither incomplete evidence nor missing declared readings may become Pass. Implementation acceptance ¶ The screen implementation ( hilt.inspector_app ) and the entry point ( hilt inspect ) follow this document. The view model is testable independently of the terminal and driven by a recorded 70-DUT rack: Reconstruct tree order, peer states, pending descendants, failure causes, timeout evidence, and missing declared readings from version-1 records alone. Navigate failures and load the selected node's own or rolled-up timeline immediately, with correct owner and scope; never show stale content after a cursor change. Open numbered pointers, group artifacts by type, and compare captures using the specified keys, including the two-artifact index collision. Preserve complete lines under truncation and distinguish unavailable evidence, malformed records, unsupported versions, and nodes that never ran. Make Inspect usable from saved evidence without source or hardware, hidden passes included; it never waits for a suite. The saved-view command and discovery rule are the ones under "Opening a run". Verify moved-run resolution preserves the complete run-relative path and remains under the opened root. Exercise captures with identical basenames in different nodes, an unestablished root mapping, and unavailable files; preserve the recorded reference in every unavailable diagnostic and never substitute another capture. Hold Re-Run to its ruling. Its adapter accepts only an operator-supplied suite through the command line ( suite_target or --suite ), never reconstruction from evidence or neighboring source, and refuses a suite whose declared tree differs from the saved one. Execution is TestComponent.run(subtree=...) : ancestors' own lifecycle, the pressed subtree, every other leaf pending. Ancestor-configure replay stays prohibited. A node above the pressed one shows partly re-run , never the state it rolled up over the one child the bench ran. Scratch evidence is replaced per node and removed on close. A live re-run holds Tab, and quitting it goes through the operator-interrupt path to Aborted with bounded cleanup before the Inspector exits. If the message, chronology, and captures do not establish a recovery category, keep the run directory and escalate with the selected node's path. The Inspector must make that uncertainty visible. Evidence earns a conclusion; the screen cannot supply one for it. Migration references ¶ The behavioral reference is the read-only hilt-test-legacy/docs/inspector.md , with navigation checked against src/inspector/InspectTab.mts , RunTab.mts , TreePanel.mts , DebugView.mts , and ArtifactModal.mts in that repository. The guide's workflow, split panes, Run tab, tree glyphs, owner arrow, failure navigation, modal, and diff controls are retained; the Failures list became the h key. Python record names, the five current categories, instance-local ctx, explicit evidence, and interruption semantics follow this port's contracts. No TypeScript runtime or language-server behavior is required to specify this saved-evidence viewer.
